title: Dallas Mavericks health ledger
deck: Dallas's health state should be tracked as dated public milestones, not converted into diagnoses or false-precision games-played forecasts.
headings: The ledger is a decision system, not an injury list
Three variables that must stay separate
text: Dallas's health state should be tracked as dated public milestones, not converted into diagnoses or false-precision games-played forecasts. Up: [[Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 season]] · Scenarios: [[Dallas Mavericks availability scenarios]] · Method: [[Availability risk in NBA projections]] Current state This ledger records the latest public evidence available to Rome as of July 10, 2026. “Official” means a league or team record. “Reported” means attributable reporting that has not been confirmed in a team medical update. “Inference” identifies basketball consequences rather than medical conclusions. Player Latest verified milestone Evidence class What is unknown Forecast consequence Kyrie Irving Dallas ruled him out for the remainder of 2025-26 while he continued recovery from March 2025 left-knee ACL reconstruction; later NBA and team material described an expectation that he could be ready for 2026-27 Official organizational chronology Full-contact clearance, preseason workload, back-to-back policy, opening-night status, and restored effectiveness Keep separate participation, workload, and effectiveness branches; transfer creation to Flagg, Nembhard, Sasser, and other connectors when Irving is limited Dereck Lively II Right-foot surgery ended his 2025-26 season after seven appearances; an attributable June 26 report said he was out of the boot and walking, swimming, and lifting but had not been cleared to run Official surgery chronology plus reported functional milestone Running, basketball activity, contact, practice clearance, preseason availability, and workload Maintain available, restricted, and unavailable center matrices; do not give his defensive and passing functions automatically to one replacement No other current Dallas player has a publicly documented health issue in Rome's sources that warrants a permanent row as of this review. That is not a claim that every player is medically unrestricted. It means the committee lacks a consequential, current, attributable milestone suitable for a durable ledger. Once the regular season begins, official NBA injury reports should govern daily designations; short-lived entries should be appended as dated deltas only when they materially change role or forecast state. Kyrie Irving chronology March 2025 — Official: Irving sustained a left-knee ACL injury. February 2026 — Official: Dallas announced he would not return during the 2025-26 season. 2026 offseason — Official organizational expectation: NBA draft and Dallas coaching material treated Irving as part of the coming season's foundation and expressed an expectation of readiness. This is planning evidence, not competitive clearance. Current classification — Unknown: Rome has no cited public evidence here of unrestricted five-on-five participation, a preseason minute plan, or an opening-night determination. The basketball implication is developed in [[Kyrie Irving return from ACL reconstruction]]. Dallas needs branches for absence, controlled participation, and functionally normal participation because an “active” designation does not establish prior burst, rim pressure, defensive movement, or workload. Dereck Lively II chronology January 2025 — Official: Dallas announced a right-ankle stress fracture, part of the longer availability context but not the same injury as the later right-foot surgery. 2025 offseason and early 2025-26 — Official: Team accounts described a foot procedure and early-season minute restrictions. November 2025 — Official: Lively returned from a knee-related absence in limited minutes. December 2025 — Official: Dallas and NBA.com reported season-ending right-foot surgery. April 15, 2026 — Official team feature: Lively was described in the recovery process after surgery, with training camp discussed as a hope rather than a clearance. June 26, 2026 — Reported: An attributable report said he was out of the boot, walking, swimming, and lifting, but not cleared to run. Current classification — Unknown: There is no later cited official functional milestone in Rome establishing running, contact, or unrestricted basketball work. The forecast consequence is explained in [[Dereck Lively II health and defensive value]] and [[Dallas center rotation without full Lively availability]]. A center-minute replacement does not by itself replace Lively's combination of rim deterrence, coverage mobility, vertical spacing, screening, and connective passing. The ledger is a decision system, not an injury list An injury list answers who appears on a report. A decision ledger answers what the public evidence permits Dallas analysts to change. That distinction matters in July, when there is no daily injury report and the strongest public signals arrive irregularly through team releases, press conferences, training footage, and attributable reporting. A roster grid may list a player normally even though his competitive workload remains unknown. Silence may mean that rehabilitation is proceeding privately, not that the player is fully available. Each row should therefore preserve five independent fields. Event state records what happened: injury, surgery, return, restriction, recurrence, or removal from a report. Functional milestone records the highest public basketball-relevant activity, such as running, individual work, controlled contact, full practice, or game participation. Source class distinguishes an official transaction or injury report from attributable reporting and inference. Decision consequence states which Dallas minutes or functions must branch. Expiration condition says what new evidence would supersede the row. This structure prevents two opposite errors. The optimistic error treats an expected return, a roster listing, or a workout clip as proof of normal availability. The pessimistic error freezes the worst historical state even after a newer official milestone changes it. A dated ledger should be conservative about interpretation and aggressive about accepting better evidence. It preserves the earlier state for audit while allowing the current classification to move. The same system also limits medical overreach. Public basketball analysis does not need to diagnose tissue, estimate individualized reinjury probability, or reverse-engineer surgical details. It needs to know which participation and role assumptions are supported. “Not cleared to run on June 26” is a legitimate dated state. “Will miss opening night” is not unless an authoritative source says so. “Expected to be ready” is organizational planning evidence. “Will immediately recover prior defensive mobility” is a forecast that requires later basketball observation. Three variables that must stay separate Health enters a team forecast through at least three variables: participation, workload, and effectiveness. Combining them into one “healthy” flag hides the most important Dallas uncertainty. Participation asks whether the player appears at all. Official active status or game participation resolves this for one date, not for a month or season. A player can be active after missing the previous game, then sit on the second night of a back-to-back. The ledger should record the sequence rather than convert one appearance into a season assumption. Workload asks what Dallas is willing to demand conditional on participation. Minutes, stint length, practice frequency, back-to-back decisions, travel, and high-intensity possessions all belong here. A 24-minute Irving appearance and a 34-minute appearance are not equivalent for team construction. A 16-minute Lively return may still provide meaningful rim protection while leaving Gafford as the stable center base. Effectiveness asks which basketball functions have returned within the available workload. Irving can be active and shoot well while producing less rim pressure or defensive change of direction. Lively can be active and finish lobs while Dallas protects him with conservative screen coverage. Those observations do not establish a medical problem; they establish the basketball version Dallas currently has. Effectiveness should be evaluated across repeated possessions and opponents, with normal small-sample caution. The three variables are related but not interchangeable. A forecast can assign an appearance branch without assuming old minutes, and assign minutes without restoring old per-minute impact. [[Availability risk in NBA projections]] provides the general method; this ledger supplies the dated Dallas inputs. Joint scenarios for Dallas Irving and Lively affect different parts of the possession, so their states should be crossed rather than modeled as isolated deductions. The purpose is not to attach false probabilities. It is to show which dependencies move together. Both functionally available This is Dallas's widest strategic branch. Irving can organize difficult half-court possessions, while Lively can anchor the basket area and turn stops into early offense. Flagg can develop as a co-creator instead of being forced into every late-clock task. Gafford can remain a high-energy complement rather than the only proven traditional center. May can test larger lineups without asking one group to solve every offensive and defensive problem. Even this branch is not a guarantee of continuity. Two players returning from long absences may receive controlled workloads, and a new coaching staff must establish roles. “Both active” is therefore weaker than “both sustaining their intended functions through repeated games.” Irving limited, Lively functionally available Dallas retains a credible defensive backbone but faces a creation shortage. Flagg, Nembhard, Sasser, Aldama, and other connectors must generate or extend advantages. Lively's screening, rim running, and short-roll decisions can make those guards' jobs easier, yet he does not replace Irving's handle or late-clock shotmaking. The team may defend well enough to create transition opportunities while remaining vulnerable when opponents force set half-court possessions. Irving available, Lively limited Dallas can organize offense around its best veteran creator, but the center allocation changes. Gafford becomes the dependable base, smaller groups must rebound collectively, and Dallas may need more conservative perimeter pressure to protect the rim. Irving's offense can reduce the number of empty possessions; it does not reproduce Lively's coverage range or defensive communication. Closing lineups become opponent-specific rather than automatic. Both limited This is not merely the sum of two replacement-minute deductions. Flagg faces more creation responsibility while also carrying large defensive assignments. Gafford's workload rises, frontcourt combinations lose flexibility, and May has fewer ways to hide a weak link. Young guards and centers may receive development minutes, but those minutes should not be projected as seamless functional replacement. This branch creates the greatest risk that role expansion changes several players' efficiency at once. These scenarios explain why [[Dallas Mavericks model pressure points]] should ingest evidence from this ledger without pretending to rerun a private model. The public conclusion is directional: joint limitations widen the distribution of Dallas outcomes and make teammate projections more correlated. Evidence hierarchy for future updates The official NBA injury report should control daily game designations once reporting begins. A Dallas release, direct press conference, or official practice-status statement can establish a milestone outside that system. Full participant comments from the player or coach are useful when quoted directly, although the exact scope of “full” should still be recorded. Attributable beat reporting can add functional detail that the club has not published, but the ledger must label it reported rather than official. Selected workout videos are discovery evidence. They can suggest a question—running, cutting, contact, or workload—but cannot establish that the activity was unrestricted, representative, medically cleared, or repeatable. Anonymous posts, unsourced screenshots, aggregator rewrites, and fantasy blurbs without attributable reporting do not establish a new state. A secondary page that clearly names the original reporter may preserve a milestone when the original article is inaccessible, but the chain and its limitation belong in the source note. Absence of evidence also needs discipline. If a player disappears from public discussion, keep the last verified milestone dated and mark the present state unknown. Do not write “still not running” two weeks after a report said he had not yet run unless a newer source confirms that condition. The ledger's wording should make the date carry the claim. Translation into minutes and roles Every accepted update should trigger a small, explicit translation review. For Irving, inspect primary initiation, late-clock creation, pull-up gravity, closing groups, and the development burden placed on Flagg and the smaller guards. For Lively, inspect center minutes, screen coverage, rim deterrence, rebounding assignments, vertical spacing, and short-roll connection. The review asks which branch changed; it does not invent a numeric wins delta. A return milestone may narrow uncertainty without immediately moving projected minutes. Running is more informative than walking, full practice is more informative than individual work, and repeated games are more informative than one appearance. Conversely, a formal restriction may change workload before it changes the probability of participation. The ledger should route those effects to [[Dallas Mavericks roster and minutes ledger]], [[Dallas Mavericks availability scenarios]], and the relevant player analysis rather than duplicating whole arguments here. This translation also protects teammate evaluation. If Flagg's usage rises while Irving is limited, the change may reflect roster necessity rather than a clean skill leap. If Dallas's rim defense declines while Lively is out, the effect cannot automatically be assigned to the substitute center because perimeter pressure and lineup context also change. Health state is part of the causal environment in which performance is observed. Update protocol Add a dated line only when the source changes a meaningful state: surgery or confirmed injury, a stated timetable, running, individual basketball work, contact work, full practice, game availability, a formal restriction, recurrence, or removal from the injury report. Preserve old milestones so later optimism does not erase the evidence available to an earlier forecast. For each update, record four separate items: what the source actually says; whether it is official, reported, inferred, or unknown; what stage changed—participation, workload, or effectiveness; which minutes and roles move in the Dallas scenario matrix. Do not infer recovery from social clips, roster listings, silence, or an absence from an offseason event. Do not turn a coach's optimism into clearance. Conversely, do not preserve an old negative milestone as current after a newer official functional update supersedes it. Why it matters Irving and Lively are not interchangeable injury rows. Irving controls the roster's highest-leverage creation task; Lively controls a bundle of center and defensive functions. Their joint status changes the value of teammates, not only the number of replacement minutes. The ledger exists to keep those dependencies dated and auditable while leaving medical judgments to qualified sources. Sources Mavericks announce Kyrie Irving will miss the remainder of 2025-26 — official Dallas release; accessed July 10, 2026. NBA report on Irving's 2025-26 absence — NBA.com chronology; accessed July 10, 2026. Dallas 2026 NBA Draft team profile — organizational roster context and return expectation; accessed July 10, 2026. NBA.com: Mavericks' Dereck Lively II to undergo season-ending surgery — official surgery chronology; accessed July 10, 2026. Dallas: Chandler knows what navigating a serious injury is like for Lively — official team recovery context, April 15, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Christian Clark recovery report, relayed by FantasyPros — attributable June 26 functional milestone; accessed July 10, 2026; treated as reported, not official. Open questions When do Irving and Lively first participate in unrestricted contact work? Will Dallas disclose workload or back-to-back restrictions before the regular season? Which official functional milestones should trigger changes to the public forecast branches? How should short-lived in-season designations be archived without turning this ledger into a news dump?

title: Dallas Mavericks model pressure points
deck: Dallas's forecast is most sensitive not to one headline talent estimate but to correlated assumptions about Kyrie Irving's functional return, Dereck Lively II's workload, Cooper Flagg's creation burden, and whether the new roster's frontcourt depth can coexist with enough guard pressure and shooting.
headings: Pressure point one: Irving is three variables, not one
Pressure point two: Lively changes the permission structure
Pressure point three: Flagg's upside can be confused with overload
Pressure point four: Aldama adds options, not automatic value
Pressure point five: secondary guards determine the floor
Pressure point six: coaching changes the context before it changes the rating
The scenario grid that should replace a single depth chart
text: Dallas's forecast is most sensitive not to one headline talent estimate but to correlated assumptions about Kyrie Irving's functional return, Dereck Lively II's workload, Cooper Flagg's creation burden, and whether the new roster's frontcourt depth can coexist with enough guard pressure and shooting. Up: [[Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 season]] · Baseline: [[Basketball/NBA team briefings 2026-27/DAL_2026_27_briefing|Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 Research Briefing]] · Inputs: [[Dallas Mavericks roster and minutes ledger]] · [[Dallas Mavericks health ledger]] · Method: [[NBA player forward projection model]] Current state as of 2026-07-10 This article is a public-safe translation layer, not a model release. It does not disclose private files, formulas, player coefficients, simulation weights, or a new win total. It asks a narrower question: which verified public developments should force a forecaster to reconsider minutes, roles, player factors, lineup interactions, or the width of the team-outcome distribution? Four facts define the current stress test. First, Dallas officially acquired Santi Aldama and Marcus Sasser, along with Tarik Biberovic's NBA rights, on July 8 while sending out Khris Middleton and AJ Johnson plus draft compensation. Second, the official Dallas roster grid still lagged that transaction when checked July 10, so the transaction announcement—not the stale grid—is the controlling event source. Third, Dallas ruled Kyrie Irving out for all of 2025-26 while he continued recovering from left-knee ACL reconstruction; later official-facing material expressed an expectation that he could be ready for 2026-27, but no reviewed source establishes unrestricted participation. Fourth, Dereck Lively II's 2025-26 season ended after seven games and right-foot surgery, with the last public milestone reviewed here not establishing a normal offseason workload. The roster has therefore improved in some visible ways without becoming easy to forecast. Aldama adds size, shooting, and connective passing. Sasser adds another guard who can handle and score. Cooper Flagg enters year two after winning Rookie of the Year. Dusty May has articulated a faster, passing-oriented identity. Yet Irving remains the only rostered player with a long NBA record as an elite primary half-court creator, while Lively remains the center with the clearest combination of rim protection, mobility, vertical spacing, and connective upside. The most important assumptions are correlated: one player's absence changes the role and efficiency environment of several others. Evidence labels and forecast language This note uses four labels deliberately. Fact means a dated public source establishes the transaction, performance record, health announcement, or organizational statement. A fact can still be incomplete. “Acquired” establishes team control; it does not establish an October rotation. “Expected to be ready” records an expectation; it does not establish clearance. Inference means a basketball consequence follows plausibly from the fact but has not yet been observed in 2026-27 competition. For example, more Irving absence should increase Flagg's initiation burden. That is a role inference, not proof that Flagg's efficiency will rise or fall by a particular amount. Unknown means the public record does not justify a settled input. Exact games played, minute restrictions, back-to-back policy, opening-night lineups, and the effectiveness of May's system are unknown. Model pressure means the evidence should prompt a sensitivity test or a changed assumption class. It does not mean the public fact can be converted honestly into a precise number of wins. A claimed “plus 2.3 wins” without a documented rerun, uncertainty interval, and interaction treatment would manufacture precision. The correct output is therefore a pressure map: what moves, in which direction, through what mechanism, and what future evidence could confirm or reverse the move. Pressure map Public input Minutes pressure Role or factor pressure Team-outcome pressure What remains unknown Irving returning from ACL reconstruction Restores some high-leverage guard minutes; range must remain broad Raises primary creation and late-clock shot quality; may lower Flagg's emergency usage Upside, but highly nonlinear with workload and effectiveness Clearance, burst, rim pressure, defense, back-to-backs, sustained load Lively returning from foot surgery Reclaims center minutes from Gafford, Aldama-at-five, and depth Raises defensive-anchor, screening, lob, and lineup-continuity expectations Upside through both defense and offensive role fit Running/contact milestones, camp participation, restriction, recurrence Flagg's second-year development Stable major minutes if available Creation, shooting gravity, turnovers, and defensive burden can move separately Largest healthy-roster developmental upside; also major overload risk Which gains are skill versus easier context Aldama acquisition and knee recovery Adds forward minutes and conditional center minutes Improves spacing and connective passing; center deployment may lower rim protection Expands lineup ceiling and matchup flexibility, conditional on health and fit Clearance, defensive assignment, sustainable center share Sasser acquisition Competes for reserve guard and some creation minutes Adds scoring and handling, but primary-creator capacity is unproven in Dallas Depth stabilizer more than automatic ceiling raiser Role, efficiency at higher usage, fit beside other small guards Middleton and AJ Johnson departures Removes wing and developmental minutes from the prior state Changes shooting, size, experience, and usage allocation Cannot be evaluated as incoming talent minus outgoing talent alone Final rotation replacements and closing-group hierarchy Dusty May installation Redistributes transition and half-court touches Pace, passing, role clarity, and coverage choices may change player context Wider early-season uncertainty before system evidence exists Actual NBA scheme, lineup preferences, execution quality Pressure point one: Irving is three variables, not one Fact: Dallas announced in February that Irving would miss the remainder of 2025-26 while continuing ACL rehabilitation. NBA and Mavericks material later described him as expected to return for 2026-27 and as a foundation for May's team. The reviewed evidence does not establish full-contact clearance, unrestricted five-on-five work, an opening-night minute target, or a back-to-back policy. Inference: Irving changes Dallas even before he approaches his old box-score production because he supplies scarce possession functions. He can bring the ball up under pressure, create the first defensive rotation, make a pull-up punish a defender who goes under, and produce a credible late-clock attempt when the designed action fails. Those functions improve the shots available to Lively, Daniel Gafford, Aldama, shooters, and cutters. They also allow Flagg to attack more tilted floors rather than beginning every difficult possession against five set defenders. Model pressure: separate Irving into participation, workload, and effectiveness variables. Games active should not mechanically restore old per-minute value. A controlled 22-minute role could have considerable lineup value if concentrated around creation-needy units and closing possessions; 30 nominal minutes could disappoint if change-of-direction, rim pressure, or defensive movement remains impaired. The model should also avoid treating Irving's minutes as independent of teammates' rates. His presence can lower Flagg's usage while improving Flagg's efficiency, increase a rolling center's finishing opportunities, and make an offense-first spacer easier to play. Wins logic: Irving creates the largest direct upside branch, but the relationship should curve rather than move linearly. The first reliable creator minutes may be more valuable than later replacement minutes because they prevent the roster from assigning primary jobs to secondary players. At the same time, a 34-year-old guard returning after an extended absence deserves a wide effectiveness band. The proper forecast response is more scenario width, not an all-or-nothing “healthy Kyrie” switch. Unknown: when he will be cleared, what workload Dallas chooses, whether he can repeatedly turn the corner, and how often he can defend NBA actions without being protected. Training camp and preseason can answer participation and role questions; only repeated competitive possessions can answer effectiveness. Pressure point two: Lively changes the permission structure Fact: Lively played only seven games in 2025-26 before season-ending right-foot surgery. Public Dallas material has described rehabilitation and hope for the coming season, but the evidence reviewed for [[Dereck Lively II health and defensive value]] does not justify assuming unrestricted training-camp work. Inference: Lively's value is not confined to blocks, rebounds, or center minutes. A credible back-line defender gives perimeter teammates permission to crowd ballhandlers, fight over screens, and send drives toward help. His mobility can preserve more coverage options than a stationary drop-only center. Offensively, his screening and lob threat create a vertical constraint, while his passing can keep an advantage alive. Those jobs let Gafford remain an energetic second center and let Aldama play more often as a skilled forward rather than as an emergency defensive five. Model pressure: build at least three Lively workload states: unavailable, restricted, and functionally normal. Each state needs a different minute matrix. An unavailable Lively raises Gafford's workload, increases Aldama-at-center or depth-center exposure, and transfers rebounding and rim-protection duties to Flagg, P. J. Washington, and the wings. A restricted Lively may still improve selected lineups without supporting an ordinary starter projection. A normal state raises both his minutes and the compatibility of teammates' roles. The factor adjustment should not award his full defensive influence twice. If the player projection already captures some rim and lineup value, a separate team-defense adjustment must represent only the interaction that the underlying method omits. Conversely, a box-score-heavy prior may understate the permission structure. [[RAPM]] and lineup evidence can help interrogate the prior, but neither should be imported without sample, teammate, opponent, and role context. Wins logic: Lively's return raises the ceiling most when it keeps multiple other players in appropriate roles. That makes his value correlated with Gafford, Aldama, and Flagg. The downside is also matchup-dependent: Dallas can cover nominal center minutes without him, but not every substitute lineup preserves rim deterrence, switching tolerance, rebounding, passing, and vertical gravity at once. Unknown: running and contact milestones, camp repetition, sustainable stint length, and which coverages May asks him to play. A positive quote without a functional milestone should move confidence less than repeated full practices or preseason games. Pressure point three: Flagg's upside can be confused with overload Fact: Flagg won the 2025-26 Rookie of the Year award after carrying a major role for Dallas. The official record establishes production and recognition; it does not establish the size or shape of a second-year leap. Inference: Flagg is the highest-leverage healthy-roster development variable because he can affect both sides and multiple possession types. Improvement could arrive through better pull-up and catch shooting, more efficient drives, stronger passing reads, fewer live-ball turnovers, improved defensive discipline, or simply better lineup context. These are not interchangeable. A scoring increase caused by more emergency possessions is different from a shooting or decision-making gain at similar difficulty. Model pressure: decompose the “year-two jump.” Minutes may remain high without changing. Offensive role should branch with Irving availability. Shooting gravity should depend not only on percentage but on volume, location, and defender response. Playmaking should distinguish creating the first advantage from making the next pass. Defensive value should account for assignment difficulty and whether Lively or another center protects the back line. The critical correlation is burden. If Irving is functional, Flagg can grow as a co-creator, screener, transition initiator, and second-side attacker. If Irving is limited, Flagg may accumulate more on-ball events while facing loaded defenses and late clocks. A naive model may read higher usage as development or apply the same efficiency curve in both contexts. The pressure test should instead ask whether his role is becoming more valuable or merely larger. Wins logic: a real creation-and-shooting leap would lift Dallas's ceiling because it reduces dependence on one veteran guard and permits more large defensive lineups. But overload could lower efficiency, increase turnovers, and consume defensive energy. Flagg is therefore both an upside driver and the main conduit through which other injuries become nonlinear. Unknown: the balance May chooses among initiation, screening, transition, and defensive assignments; whether defenders honor the jumper; and whether improved outcomes persist after controlling for Irving and lineup context. Pressure point four: Aldama adds options, not automatic value Fact: Dallas officially acquired Aldama on July 8. NBA statistics show that he brought credible three-point volume, passing production, and frontcourt size in 2025-26. His official player-news chronology also records a season-ending right-knee procedure in March, so unrestricted fall availability is not established by the trade. Inference: Aldama's cleanest base role is skilled forward beside Lively or Gafford. His shooting can pull a frontcourt defender from the lane; his passing can extend an advantage; his size can preserve rebounding and finishing. At center he can create five-out spacing and force slow bigs to defend away from the rim, but Dallas then transfers rim protection, physical box-outs, and some containment work to the rest of the lineup. Model pressure: do not enter Aldama as a uniform talent upgrade. Assign separate forward and center shares, each conditioned on his health and Lively's availability. His offensive factor may rise in lineups with an advantage creator and a rolling center, while his defensive factor can vary sharply by assignment. Center minutes may improve spacing but worsen rim defense or rebounding. Forward minutes may preserve role fit but compress minutes for Washington, Naji Marshall, or other large wings. Wins logic: Aldama expands the number of viable lineup solutions, which can raise the matchup ceiling and reduce the cost of some injuries. Optionality has value only if the coach can identify combinations that cover all five jobs. It is not equal to adding each player's isolated estimate. [[Lineup fit is not the sum of player value]] is the governing principle. Unknown: clearance after the knee procedure, his base defensive assignment, how frequently May uses him at center, and whether opponents guard his shot tightly enough to create the intended space. Pressure point five: secondary guards determine the floor Fact: Dallas acquired Marcus Sasser and retained other handling options including Ryan Nembhard and secondary initiators on the wing. Tyus Jones is not a current Maverick. No public source establishes that any non-Irving guard can reproduce Irving's complete creation role. Inference: Sasser can add pull-up willingness, scoring, and ballhandling; Nembhard can help organize possessions; Christie, Marshall, Aldama, and Flagg can extend advantages or initiate selected actions. Collectively, that group can cover ball-touch volume. Covering touches is not the same as creating efficient shots against a set defense. The distinction matters most when Irving sits and opponents load toward Flagg. Model pressure: transferred minutes should carry transferred difficulty. Promoting a reserve scorer into primary creation should not preserve his lower-usage efficiency automatically. Similarly, a connector's assist rate should not be projected as though he will generate the first advantage. The rotation should distinguish organizer, advantage creator, secondary attacker, movement shooter, and defensive guard rather than collapsing all of them into “backcourt minutes.” Wins logic: the secondary guards govern Dallas's floor more than its theoretical ceiling. Competent non-Irving organization can prevent disastrous bench possessions, protect Flagg from constant pressure, and activate finishers. A genuine breakout creator would create further upside, but the public evidence does not support building that into the central case. Unknown: Sasser's Dallas role, Nembhard's effectiveness against starter pressure, the guard pairings May trusts, and which player closes when Irving is unavailable or managed. Pressure point six: coaching changes the context before it changes the rating Fact: Dallas hired Dusty May in June. His official introduction emphasized pace, passing, adaptable offense, and accountability. He has not coached a Dallas regular-season game. Inference: those principles fit a roster with a grab-and-go forward in Flagg, multiple passing bigs, rim-running centers, and uncertain point-guard availability. Early offense can reduce the number of possessions that begin against a set defense. Multiple ball screens and rapid reversals can let Aldama and Flagg attack a moving defense. Defensive adaptability can exploit Dallas's size. Model pressure: avoid a generic “new coach bump.” Coaching initially widens uncertainty because role allocation, substitution patterns, pace, and coverages change the context of every player rate. A model can test tactical implications—more transition opportunities, different usage shares, more or fewer two-big minutes—without assigning May an unsupported standalone win value. Wins logic: scheme can reduce the frequency of Dallas's hardest problems, but it cannot erase missing skills. Pace does not replace late-clock creation. Switching does not create a rim protector. Passing does not help if no player bends the first defender. May's influence should emerge through observed role and lineup evidence, not reputation. Unknown: actual NBA pace, who initiates, which frontcourt combinations close, how often Dallas switches, and whether the intended principles survive opponents' scouting. The scenario grid that should replace a single depth chart The public record supports a compact scenario grid, not probability claims: Irving and Lively functionally available. Dallas can keep Flagg in a co-creation role, share center minutes, and use Aldama primarily as a skilled forward. This is the cleanest upside structure, but it still requires evidence of effectiveness and continuity. Irving available, Lively limited. Creation remains organized; Gafford absorbs traditional-center work and Aldama supplies selective five-out minutes. Defensive and rebounding matchup variance rises. Lively available, Irving limited. Dallas retains a defensive skeleton but asks Flagg and the secondary guards to manufacture offense. Shooting around the creators becomes more important. Both limited. Role cascades compound: Flagg carries more creation and defense, Gafford's workload rises, Aldama fills more structural gaps, and reserve guards face harder possessions. This is the nonlinear downside case. Both active but below old effectiveness. The most easily missed branch. Binary availability looks positive while burst, workload, coverage range, or continuity remains below the prior assumption. Each branch should have its own minute matrix and role definitions. Only after reliable evidence exists should a forecast assign weights. Even then, the outputs should show a range and describe what drives it. The previous Dallas briefing can remain a dated baseline; this page records why the next rerun may move and why a judgmental adjustment must never be presented as a completed rerun. Verification triggers The pressure map should update when evidence changes, not when optimism or anxiety becomes louder. For Irving, meaningful positive triggers include full-contact practice, repeated preseason participation, demonstrated rim pressure and change-of-direction, and ordinary rather than exceptional workload management. For Lively, they include running, basketball activity, full contact, repeated practice, and sustained movement through defensive coverages. For Aldama, they include clearance after the knee procedure and evidence of the defensive role Dallas intends. For Flagg and the guards, the best evidence is role-based: who initiates against a set defense, who draws two defenders, what happens after the first action, and how efficiency changes by lineup. For May, track possession style and lineup choices rather than press-conference vocabulary. Once games begin, official NBA injury reports establish availability designations; film and statistics explain role and performance but should state the sample and context. Negative triggers include delayed clearance, repeated non-contact status, a stated restriction extending into the season, role promotions that reduce efficiency, and lineup families that cannot defend the rim or create a first advantage. A single practice clip, made jumper, block, or preseason plus-minus is weak evidence. Why this framing matters Dallas's roster is deep in bodies and broad in possible lineups, but it is not redundant in its most important functions. Irving owns the clearest elite-creator history. Lively offers the most complete two-way center concept. Flagg connects the present roster to the next competitive window. Aldama and Sasser add real optionality while bringing new health, role, and fit questions. May can reorganize the environment, but his system is still a hypothesis. A useful forecast respects that structure. It separates minutes from role, participation from effectiveness, and individual value from lineup interaction. It recognizes that the same Flagg usage can mean healthy development in one branch and emergency overload in another. It lets a Lively return affect not only his own projection but also Gafford's workload, Aldama's position, and the perimeter's defensive behavior. It credits Irving's ability to improve other players' shot environments without pretending any return recreates his prior self automatically. The result is less theatrical than a precise win-delta headline and more useful. The public can see which assumptions matter, which direction each would push, and which observations would falsify the story. The private model can remain private. When the next verified roster, health, or role fact arrives, Dallas's forecast should change through an explicit causal path rather than through an unexplained manual number. Which player initiates the majority of half-court possessions when Irving sits, and who creates the first advantage rather than merely organizing? Does May use Aldama primarily beside a traditional center or as the center in five-out groups? title: Dallas Mavericks roster and minutes ledger
deck: Dallas has enough verified personnel to map its 2026-27 rotation, but not enough health or contract certainty to publish one fixed depth chart: the honest ledger uses status tiers and conditional minute ranges.
headings: Verified basketball core and status boundary
Forecast branch A — Irving and Lively functionally available
Forecast branch B — Irving active but managed
Forecast branch C — Lively delayed or restricted
Forecast branch D — both high-leverage players unavailable
text: Dallas has enough verified personnel to map its 2026-27 rotation, but not enough health or contract certainty to publish one fixed depth chart: the honest ledger uses status tiers and conditional minute ranges. Up: [[Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 season]] · Baseline: [[Basketball/NBA team briefings 2026-27/DAL_2026_27_briefing|Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 Research Briefing]] · Health: [[Dallas Mavericks health ledger]] · Scenarios: [[Dallas Mavericks availability scenarios]] The controlling roster record The first job of a roster ledger is identity, not projection. Dallas officially announced on July 8 that it acquired Santi Aldama, Marcus Sasser, and the NBA rights to Tarik Biberovic in a six-team transaction. The Mavericks sent out Khris Middleton and AJ Johnson, as well as draft compensation. The NBA's offseason trade tracker independently records the completed transaction. Those dated event records control even though the Mavericks' public roster grid still displayed Middleton and Johnson and omitted Aldama and Sasser when checked July 10. That conflict is a publication lag, not evidence that the trade was reversed. A roster page is a useful display, but a dated transaction announcement is the stronger source for whether a transaction occurred. The NBA player pages already identify Aldama and Sasser with Dallas, adding a second official cross-check. Therefore this ledger assigns no Dallas role or minutes to Middleton or Johnson and includes Aldama and Sasser in the basketball inventory. One correction is especially important because stale depth charts can propagate quickly: Tyus Jones is not a current Maverick. Dallas's official 2025-26 game notes record that it waived Jones on February 28 after an eight-game Dallas stint. Denver then announced his signing on March 5, and official Nuggets game notes list him on Denver's roster. Assigning Jones Dallas minutes would be a factual roster error, not a debatable forecast choice. The ledger also separates NBA employment from rights ownership. Dallas acquiring Biberovic's NBA rights does not establish an NBA contract, a roster place, or availability for training camp. The same caution applies to other draft-rights players. A summer-league appearance, draft selection, camp invitation, two-way deal, Exhibit 10 agreement, standard contract, and guaranteed opening-night roster place are different states. Names are not interchangeable with roster slots. Evidence labels used here Official means a fact established by a team or league transaction record, contract announcement, roster record, or medical statement. Reported means credible journalism that has not been matched here to an official filing. Inference means a basketball conclusion drawn from verified personnel, roles, or past performance. Forecast means a proposed 2026-27 minute range or rotation branch. Unknown means the reviewed public evidence does not resolve the question. This distinction matters because a clean-looking depth chart can hide several different claims. “Kyrie Irving is under contract,” “Irving is expected back,” “Irving will be active on opening night,” and “Irving will play 32 minutes at his prior level” are not one proposition. Only the first two are supported in the reviewed official record. The participation date, workload, back-to-back plan, and functional performance remain unknown. Verified basketball core and status boundary The following table is a working basketball inventory, not a representation of a finalized 15-man roster. “Rotation claim” identifies what can responsibly be said today. Player or asset Verified state Rotation claim as of July 10 Kyrie Irving Official Dallas guard; missed all of 2025-26 while continuing ACL rehabilitation Core creator if active; exact return date, workload, and effectiveness unknown Cooper Flagg Official Dallas forward after a 70-game rookie season Core high-minute player; year-two creation share is a forecast P. J. Washington Present in the stable official roster core Core forward whose exact starting combinations remain a coaching decision Naji Marshall Present in the stable official roster core High-probability wing rotation member Max Christie Present in the stable official roster core High-probability wing rotation member with shooting and defensive value Klay Thompson Present in the stable official roster core Veteran shooting option; role size is not guaranteed by reputation Caleb Martin Present in the stable official roster core Wing depth; role depends on health, shooting, and competing combinations Dereck Lively II Official Dallas center; played seven games in 2025-26 before right-foot surgery Core center when available; readiness and workload remain unknown Daniel Gafford Present in the stable official roster core Proven center rotation member and principal Lively contingency Santi Aldama Officially acquired July 8; NBA player page identifies Dallas Rotation forward/center; exact position split is a forecast Marcus Sasser Officially acquired July 8; NBA player page identifies Dallas Candidate reserve scoring guard, not a proven replacement lead creator Ryan Nembhard Converted to a multiyear standard contract in March; Dallas exercised its 2026-27 team option June 29 Rotation organizer candidate with a verified standard-contract path Brandon Williams Appeared on the official roster display when reviewed Contract and final-role details require transaction reconciliation before assigning protected minutes Dwight Powell Appeared on the official roster display, while a league pre-draft profile treated him as a free agent Current 2026-27 contract state unresolved in the reviewed evidence John Poulakidas, Tyler Smith, Moussa Cisse and other depth names Appeared on official or established roster displays during the cycle Do not treat display presence alone as proof of final standard-roster status or rotation role Morez Johnson Jr. and other 2026 draft/development players Connected to Dallas through draft or development records Contract type, readiness, and opening-night role must be verified separately Tarik Biberovic and other draft-rights players Dallas owns NBA rights where officially recorded Rights ownership only; zero projected NBA minutes without a signing Khris Middleton and AJ Johnson Officially sent out July 8 Not Dallas rotation players despite stale roster-grid display Tyus Jones Waived by Dallas February 28; signed by Denver March 5 Not a Maverick; zero Dallas minutes The boundary is intentionally conservative. It is possible that later official processing resolves several depth contracts cleanly. It is not responsible to fill uncertainty with assumptions merely so every line of a depth chart has a name. The 240-minute accounting problem Every NBA game contains 240 player-minutes before overtime: five players multiplied by 48 regulation minutes. A useful preseason ledger allocates those minutes by role and scenario rather than pretending to predict exact season averages. Ranges should answer three questions: who has a credible rotation path, which absences force structural changes, and where competition remains open? The Dallas problem has two unusually large switches. Irving determines whether Dallas has its only proven elite half-court guard creator. Lively determines whether Dallas can build its center rotation around a mobile rim protector and vertical spacer or must lean more heavily on Gafford and offense-first frontcourt alternatives. Their statuses interact. When both are active, Dallas can pair a premier pick-and-roll creator with vertical centers and ask Flagg to attack a tilted defense. When Irving is limited, Flagg, Nembhard, Sasser, Marshall, and other connectors must create more possessions. When Lively is limited, [[Dallas center rotation without full Lively availability|the center solution]] changes the defensive and spacing responsibilities around those creators. This is why one fixed “minutes projection” would be false precision. The following branches are forecasts, not reports of coaching decisions. Forecast branch A — Irving and Lively functionally available This branch assumes both players can participate without a severe game-to-game restriction. It does not assume they immediately reproduce career-best performance. Role cluster Forecast regulation minutes Allocation logic Irving 28–32 Primary creation with deliberate workload protection after a long absence Flagg 32–35 Two-way centerpiece and co-creator; avoids making every possession his initiation test Washington, Marshall, Christie 70–82 combined Main two-way forward/wing bridge across starting and bench groups Thompson, Martin 22–36 combined Shooting and veteran wing minutes, adjusted for matchup and defensive fit Lively, Gafford 38–44 combined Most center minutes, with neither forced into an extreme workload Aldama 22–28 Skilled forward beside a center plus selective offense-first minutes at five Nembhard, Sasser and reserve guards 20–32 combined Organization, second-side shooting, and non-Irving ballhandling Remaining depth 0–12 Matchup, development, injury substitution, or earned camp competition These ranges overlap because players span clusters and because the table describes a feasible envelope, not an instruction to add every maximum. A specific nightly plan must total 240. A plausible healthy-shape example could devote roughly 31 minutes to Irving, 34 to Flagg, 29 to Washington, 27 to Marshall, 25 to Christie, 24 to Aldama, 22 to Lively, 20 to Gafford, and the remaining 28 across Thompson, Nembhard, Sasser, Martin, and matchup depth. That illustration shows the squeeze: Dallas has more credible veterans and prospects than it has stable nightly minutes. The healthy branch creates competition rather than eliminating uncertainty. Aldama can absorb minutes at both frontcourt positions, but playing him at center trades some rim protection and physical rebounding for shooting and passing. Thompson remains a unique movement-shooting threat, but he should not automatically receive closing minutes if a defensive matchup demands Christie, Marshall, or Washington. Nembhard may be the cleanest organizer behind Irving, while Sasser may supply more pull-up scoring. Their functions can coexist; neither should be labeled a complete Irving substitute. Forecast branch B — Irving active but managed “Active” may include a minute ceiling, no back-to-backs, shorter shifts, or diminished burst. None of those policies has been officially specified. If Irving plays roughly 20–28 minutes rather than a normal lead-guard load, Dallas must redistribute eight to twelve creation minutes without expecting one reserve to inherit his whole job. Flagg's on-ball work would rise first. Nembhard could organize more half-court entries and protect possession quality. Sasser could receive additional bench scoring possessions, especially beside a larger initiator. Marshall and Aldama can advance the ball, attack a closeout, and connect actions. Thompson's gravity can simplify decisions for all of them. The mechanism is distributed creation : several players replace pieces of Irving's workload, while no claim is made that they replace his handle, shot-making, rim pressure, passing manipulation, and late-clock rescue as a package. A managed-Irving plan should also stagger him from Flagg enough to stabilize bench units without depriving Flagg of reps as a primary initiator. The coaching tradeoff is development versus possession quality. Too much separation asks Irving to carry fragile lineups and increases workload. Too little separation leaves non-Irving minutes without a tested organizer and delays learning about Flagg's ceiling. [[Dallas guard creation after roster turnover]] treats this as a portfolio problem rather than a depth-chart label. Forecast branch C — Lively delayed or restricted If Lively cannot handle a normal center load, Gafford becomes the foundation rather than one half of a balanced tandem. A reasonable scenario envelope gives Gafford roughly 24–30 minutes, Aldama 6–14 situational minutes at center, and a verified depth center or small-ball group the remainder. This is not a claim that Aldama replaces Lively defensively. It is a way to cover the clock while changing the scheme. Dallas would need to redistribute Lively's functions across the lineup. Gafford supplies vertical finishing, shot blocking, screening, and physicality, but his offense is also creator-dependent. Aldama supplies shooting, passing, and five-out possibility, but lineups around him must rebound and protect the rim collectively. Washington, Flagg, Marshall, and Christie would carry more help-defense and rebounding responsibility. The team could also use matchup-specific depth, but no unverified player should receive forecast minutes simply because a roster slot appears open. The Lively branch interacts with Irving's status. Without both players, Dallas loses its cleanest creator-center partnership and cannot solve the offense by merely increasing Gafford's minutes. The ballhandler must first force the defense to react before a rim-running center can exploit the advantage. That makes Flagg development, Nembhard organization, Sasser pull-up shooting, and Aldama connectivity more important at the same time that the defense becomes harder to stabilize. Forecast branch D — both high-leverage players unavailable This is the stress case, not the baseline prediction. It should remain in the ledger because projections that omit correlated downside overstate certainty. Flagg would become the central initiator and likely the highest-minute player. Gafford would anchor conventional center minutes. Washington, Marshall, Christie, and Aldama would form the principal size-and-skill bridge. Nembhard and Sasser would compete for larger guard responsibilities, while Thompson's shooting would become even more valuable to preserve space. The stress case changes goals as well as minutes. Dallas might prioritize development and lineup discovery over squeezing every veteran minute for marginal short-term gain. That is an inference from roster age and uncertainty, not an announced organizational policy. The responsible forecast should present a performance range wide enough to reflect that choice rather than quietly assuming perfect health and win-now deployment. Rotation competitions that remain real The second organizer. Nembhard has the clearest verified organizational path, but organization is not the same as scoring pressure. Sasser's shooting and pull-up ability may fit better beside Flagg in some lineups. Dallas can use both if roles are complementary and defense holds; the competition is for specific tasks, not merely a “backup point guard” title. The wing squeeze. Marshall, Christie, Washington, Thompson, Martin, and Flagg can consume almost all non-center forward and wing minutes before Aldama is counted. The eventual allocation will reveal Dallas's priorities: movement shooting, point-of-attack defense, size, secondary handling, or development. Reputation should not settle the contest in advance. The Aldama position split. [[Santi Aldama in Dallas lineups]] argues that his cleanest base role is skilled forward beside a true center. His center minutes are still strategically important because they open the floor. The split will depend on Lively's health, Gafford's load, opponent size, and whether Dallas can defend and rebound around a lighter five. The final depth places. Official display names and development players must pass a contract-status gate before they pass a basketball gate. After that, shooting, positional size, defensive reliability, and the ability to survive low-usage minutes should determine who has a realistic role. The ledger should not reserve minutes for an unresolved contract. Update protocol This note should change when an official transaction, signing, waiver, conversion, option decision, or medical milestone changes a branch. Each update should record the event date and research date separately. A roster-grid correction can resolve the display conflict, but it should not erase the transaction chronology that explains why the earlier grid was stale. Minutes should move only after the relevant fact changes. A standard signing moves a player from rights or camp status into the NBA inventory; it does not guarantee rotation minutes. Medical clearance moves a player toward participation; it does not prove unrestricted workload or restored effectiveness. A preseason role quote is evidence of intent; it is not a binding regular-season allocation. Actual games will eventually replace forecast ranges with observed role distributions, ideally over enough possessions to avoid treating one matchup or injury substitution as a permanent hierarchy. Why it matters Roster mistakes are upstream errors. If Tyus Jones is incorrectly left on Dallas, if Middleton or Johnson remain because a stale page was scraped, or if Biberovic's rights are treated as a signed contract, every downstream lineup, cap, and team projection begins from the wrong population. Even a sophisticated player model cannot repair invalid roster inputs. Minute mistakes are equally consequential. Player value becomes team value through availability and role. A projection that gives Irving 34 unrestricted minutes and Lively a normal season without branching has embedded two optimistic medical assumptions while presenting them as arithmetic. A ledger with conditional ranges makes those assumptions visible. It connects [[NBA roster churn as projection uncertainty]] to the specific Dallas questions in [[Dallas Mavericks model pressure points]] and gives future analysis a reproducible starting point. The practical conclusion is restrained but useful: Dallas has a deep group of credible forwards and centers, a singular high-end creator whose return remains the largest swing, and several narrower guard options rather than a verified substitute for him. The team can construct a rotation today. It cannot yet justify one exact rotation. Santi Aldama NBA player page — official current-team and player-history cross-check; accessed July 10, 2026.
