title: BealeSurfaceSolver research status and open frontier
deck: BealeSurfaceSolver is an active research laboratory with a functioning geometry-general package core, a much larger experimental solver library, several manuscript programs, and important unresolved questions in analysis, stability, calibration, and publication.
headings: What is implemented in the reusable package
Strongest established threads in the repository record
Claims that remain bounded or provisional
text: BealeSurfaceSolver is an active research laboratory with a functioning geometry-general package core, a much larger experimental solver library, several manuscript programs, and important unresolved questions in analysis, stability, calibration, and publication. Up: [[BealeSurfaceSolver research (MOC)]] Snapshot status The local repository identifies the software as version , authored by Andrew Park and licensed under MIT. Its latest inspected commit is dated 2026-06-21, while the working tree contains extensive staged and untracked simulation outputs, research drivers, manuscripts, and later brown-dwarf program artifacts. This means the 2026-07-09 snapshot is an active laboratory state, not a clean tagged release. The source documents repeatedly report a green Julia suite, and package tests cover the core discretization plus promoted structure-preserving, adjoint, and oblate-figure features. This Rome import did not run the full campaign or normalize the working tree. Claims below are therefore descriptions of the repository's recorded evidence, not new independent certification. What is implemented in the reusable package smooth closed surfaces represented by built-in or functional level sets; Cartesian-grid cut-point construction and primary/secondary topology; sparse equilibration and reduced surface operators; matrix-free and sparse Laplace–Beltrami diffusion; explicit and implicit diffusion time stepping with GMRES support; Turing-style reaction–diffusion; sphere advection and Williamson shallow water; geometry-general forced-damped shallow water on arbitrary admissible level sets; generic quadrature and selected mimetic, structure-preserving, weak-Hodge, and adjoint primitives; promoted oblate, Maclaurin, and tidal-figure geometry utilities; command-line, output, and benchmark-table paths. This is already enough to make the central computational claim meaningful: the same geometry and operator machinery can run multiple PDE families on more than one surface. What exists as research infrastructure The directory contains over one hundred Julia drivers in the inspected snapshot. They range across energy-balance climate, surface modes, quasi-geostrophy, semi-Lagrangian transport, higher-order pattern equations, magnetism, moving surfaces, inverse problems, shallow-water MHD, radiative-transfer proxies, planetary applications, and cross-disciplinary surface dynamics. Breadth is not uniform maturity. Some drivers have manufactured solutions, conservation gates, parameter sweeps, independent verifier notes, and paper-ready figures. Others are demonstrators, boundary probes, or failed experiments preserved for diagnosis. The repository's result index and phase capstones are useful maps, but the strongest scientific unit remains an individual claim with its own code, parameters, saved output, verification, and caveats. Strongest established threads in the repository record Geometry-general numerical core The sphere regression, ellipsoid diffusion, geometry-general metric identity, and manufactured-solution tables support the cut-point method as a practical second-order engine over its tested smooth-surface regime. This is the mathematical spine described in [[Beale cut-point method for surface PDEs]]. Geometry-sensitive planetary PDEs The clearest positive results are those with exact or manufactured anchors and matched controls: Laplace–Beltrami mode splitting, equal-area energy-balance climate changes, forced shallow-water geometry sweeps, moving-surface demonstrations, and the one-gradient brown-dwarf lever matrix. See [[Geometry as forcing in planetary surface PDEs]]. Structure and inverse methods Later promoted modules explore mimetic operators, energy/enstrophy-preserving vorticity evolution, weak Hodge projection, and surface adjoints. These make the repository more than a catalog of forward simulations: it also contains the beginnings of long-time conservative dynamics and PDE-constrained retrieval. Claims that remain bounded or provisional There is no general convergence proof for the equilibration-reduced operator. Mixed-sign interpolation prevents a general monotonicity or positivity guarantee. Hyperbolic dynamics remain less robust than elliptic and parabolic problems, especially on extreme figures. The viscosity-free weather research path still has a checkerboard wave mode and fails on some triaxial Jacobi states. The packaged shallow-water closure omits the active-layer momentum exchange and vertical structure. Many astrophysical numbers are nondimensional or model-internal rather than calibrated predictions for measured bodies. The WASP-43b latitude problem is a bounded null, not a success of geometry alone. Several manuscripts are described as in preparation; a repository manuscript is not evidence of peer review or publication. Extensive uncommitted working artifacts make commit-level reproduction of the newest claims harder until the tree is frozen. A prioritized mathematical frontier Analysis of equilibration. Establish stability and consistency bounds for L_hE_h on a quantitative class of surfaces; determine whether a variational or energy argument can replace the unavailable maximum principle. Positivity and monotonicity. Develop a flux-limited or otherwise bound-preserving surface operator for reaction and transport problems without sacrificing geometry generality. Hyperbolic stabilization. Control the checkerboard mode and extreme-figure instability with a semi-implicit, compatible, or carefully filtered method whose dissipation is measurable rather than tuned invisibly. Moving-surface conservation. Couple cut-point rebuilding to a discrete geometric-conservation law and quantify transfer error when degrees of freedom change. Package promotion. Move only the best-verified semi-Lagrangian, climate, and higher-order primitives into , each with cold tests and stable interfaces. Frozen reproducibility. Tag a release, reduce generated-file noise, and bind every manuscript claim to a code revision, manifest, seed, and data hash. A prioritized scientific frontier Turn idealized parameter sweeps into dimensionally calibrated forecasts with uncertainty. Replace grey or proxy observables with wavelength-dependent radiative transfer where the question requires it. Separate figure, cloud, spot, and circulation signatures under realistic correlated noise. Use the solver where its geometry advantage is structural: changing topology, moving boundaries, or directly measured non-spherical figures. Treat model failure as information: specify whether a null belongs to the physical hypothesis, the closure, the diagnostic, or the numerical stability envelope. Source trail Synthesized from the package metadata, repository map, current source exports, test layout, result index, Phase-1 through Phase-5 capstones, and the brown-dwarf Program-I/III capstones in the local repository. Open questions Which two or three claims should define the first frozen public release and paper submission? Can the strong elliptic/parabolic results be published independently of the more fragile atmospheric program? What minimum external cross-validation would make the geometry-as-forcing results persuasive beyond the cut-point codebase? Which newest working-tree artifacts are canonical, and which are regenerable or superseded?

title: Equilibration in the Beale cut-point method
deck: Equilibration is the extension map that reconstructs all secondary cut-point values from the independent primary unknowns, allowing overlapping Cartesian graph charts to behave like one surface discretization.
headings: What should be verified whenever equilibration changes
text: Equilibration is the extension map that reconstructs all secondary cut-point values from the independent primary unknowns, allowing overlapping Cartesian graph charts to behave like one surface discretization. Up: [[BealeSurfaceSolver research (MOC)]] · Background: [[Beale cut-point method for surface PDEs]] The local interpolation rule Let s be a secondary cut point, p its associated primary point, and q^- and q^+ the neighboring cut points in the relevant chart direction. If the offset of s from p in grid units is \theta , with |\theta|\le 1/2 , quadratic interpolation imposes u(s) =\tfrac12(-\theta+\theta^2)u(q^-) +(1-\theta^2)u(p) +\tfrac12(\theta+\theta^2)u(q^+). The rule is exact on quadratic data along that grid line. It is also exact on constants because the three coefficients sum to one. The complication is that q^- or q^+ can themselves be secondary. Reconstruction is therefore not a sequence of independent interpolations; the secondary values are mutually coupled. The global extension operator Collect primary and secondary values into vectors u_p and u_s . The interpolation equations have the block form u_s=\Pi_{sp}u_p+\Pi_{ss}u_s, so u_s=(I-\Pi_{ss})^{-1}\Pi_{sp}u_p. This defines the equilibration or primary-to-all extension map E_h . Each row of \Pi_{ss} has absolute row sum at most 1/2 , making I-\Pi_{ss} strictly diagonally dominant in the ideal construction. That gives existence and uniqueness for the extension even when secondary dependencies form cycles. The Julia implementation analyzes those dependencies as strongly connected components. Acyclic components can be resolved in dependency order; small cyclic components are solved as local linear systems. The resulting sparse map can be cached and reused when assembling a surface operator or advancing many fields. Why it is geometry-generic Once the cut points and their chart topology have been built, equilibration does not need to evaluate \phi . It depends on offsets and neighbor relationships, not on whether the underlying surface is a sphere, ellipsoid, torus, or another admissible level set. Geometry enters later through metric weights and tangent projections. That separation is structurally valuable: \text{primary data} \xrightarrow{E_h} \text{all cut-point data} \xrightarrow{L_h} \text{local chart operator values}. The reduced operator is essentially the primary restriction of L_hE_h . A new PDE can reuse the same extension machinery if its spatial terms can be expressed through the existing chart operators. The price of mixed signs The quadratic coefficients are not all nonnegative. For one sign of \theta , one of the two outer weights is negative. Consequently, even if the unreduced differential stencil has a favorable sign pattern, its composition with E_h need not be monotone. This is why the method does not automatically inherit an M-matrix, a discrete maximum principle, or positivity preservation. The repository records a practical manifestation in reaction–diffusion work: sharp Gray–Scott interfaces could overshoot below the physical range, feeding an unstable reaction term. A clamp or a monotone alternative was required in that research path. That is evidence about a particular implementation and regime, not a proof that every equilibrated implicit solve is unstable. Robustness fallbacks create another tradeoff. When a distorted surface and coarse grid leave a missing half-stencil, the current implementation can drop the unavailable contribution while preserving constants rather than crashing. This broadens the executable geometry range, but it changes the local approximation and therefore belongs in convergence and sensitivity tests. What should be verified whenever equilibration changes Constants extend exactly. The primary values remain unchanged. Cyclic secondary components solve reproducibly. The extension is bounded as resolution and geometry change. A manufactured smooth field retains the expected convergence order after extension. Sparse assembled and matrix-free operators agree to the intended tolerance. Positivity-sensitive PDEs are tested independently rather than inferred from diffusion accuracy. Source trail Synthesized from , , , and the implementation-campaign discussion of the no-M-matrix limitation. Open questions Is there a modified interpolation with useful monotonicity that preserves geometry generality and at least second-order accuracy? Can the extension norm be bounded uniformly over a quantitative class of surfaces and grids? How much accuracy is lost by the incomplete-stencil fallback, and can that loss be localized a priori? Would a variational interpretation of equilibration make energy estimates easier than a pointwise interpretation?

title: Forced-damped shallow-water equations on a level-set surface
deck: The generalized BealeSurfaceSolver weather model evolves a thin fluid layer on any admissible level-set surface, with geometry-aware fluxes, local Coriolis force, radiative relaxation, and Rayleigh drag.
headings: What is in the package today
text:
The generalized BealeSurfaceSolver weather model evolves a thin fluid layer on any admissible level-set surface, with geometry-aware fluxes, local Coriolis force, radiative relaxation, and Rayleigh drag. Up: [[BealeSurfaceSolver research (MOC)]] · Geometry: [[Level-set geometry for surface conservation laws]] The model Let \Phi=gh be layer geopotential and v the tangential velocity. A useful forced-damped shallow-water model is \partial_t v+(v\cdot
abla_\Gamma)v +f_\Gamma n	imes v =-
abla_\Gamma\Phi- rac{v}{	au_{\mathrm{drag}}}, \partial_t\Phi+
abla_\Gamma\cdot(\Phi v) = rac{\Phi_{\mathrm{eq}}-\Phi}{	au_{\mathrm{rad}}}. Here f_\Gamma=2\Omega\cdot n, \qquad \Phi_{\mathrm{eq}}(x) = ar\Phi+\Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{eq}} \max(0,n(x)\cdot\hat s), where \hat s points toward the star. The right-hand side relaxes the layer toward a hotter dayside and a cooler nightside; Rayleigh drag removes momentum. These are deliberately idealized closures for a single active layer, not a three-dimensional atmospheric model. The package evolves momentum q=\Phi v in conservation form. In a local graph chart, both mass and momentum fluxes are multiplied by the metric factor \sqrt g , differenced, and divided by \sqrt g . Normals, tangent projections, \sqrt g , and f_\Gamma come from 
abla\phi . The same equations therefore run on spheres, oblate or triaxial ellipsoids, and other smooth closed level sets without deriving a new coordinate system for each surface. What is in the package today implements the geometry-general forced-damped equations with a MacCormack predictor-corrector core and Beale-style artificial viscosity. Its parameter object exposes the substellar direction, mean and day-night equilibrium geopotential, radiative and drag timescales, and viscosity coefficient. Taking infinite forcing timescales and a sphere recovers the unforced Williamson-test setting. The time step is conceptually: equilibrate the current primary fields to all cut points; evaluate forward-difference fluxes and pointwise sources; take the predictor step and reproject momentum tangentially; evaluate backward-difference fluxes for the corrector; add artificial viscosity, equilibrate, and reproject again. This path is simple and is regression-tested against the original sphere calculation. Its weakness is that the artificial-viscosity coefficient is a numerical modeling choice that can blur a small geometry signal. The research-grade semi-Lagrangian alternative The repository also contains standalone research implementations of a viscosity-free semi-Lagrangian transport core. A departure point is traced backward along the velocity, projected back to \Gamma , and the old field is interpolated there. A global Appendix-B quadrature rescaling fixes total mass. Repository notes report second-order manufactured-solution behavior over practical resolution ranges and machine-level relative mass drift for the tested transport problems. That alternative is scientifically important because it removes the tunable viscosity parameter. It is not equivalent to saying every semi-Lagrangian weather run is unconditionally stable: the centered gravity-wave part still has a checkerboard mode, and strongly triaxial Jacobi-figure experiments have diverged. The semi-Lagrangian weather engine largely remains research infrastructure rather than the single canonical package entry point. Verification anchors The generic MacCormack path reproduces the specialized Williamson-2 sphere errors closely: the repository reports L_2(\Phi)=1.115	imes10^{-2} at N=80 and 2.991	imes10^{-3} at N=160 , versus Beale table values 1.13	imes10^{-2} and 3.03	imes10^{-3} . The generic-versus-specialized difference shrinks with refinement. Manufactured-solution studies of the geometry-general flux report approximately second-order convergence on sphere, oblate, and strongly triaxial surfaces. A sharp \max(0,n\cdot\hat s) terminator can reduce observed order because the equilibrium field is only continuous; resolving a smooth transition restores the expected order in the recorded experiments. The forced model also reproduces the intended qualitative hot-Jupiter controls: shorter radiative time produces a larger day-night contrast, and the flow develops an eastward equatorial jet and Matsuno-Gill-like gyres. These are validation targets for model behavior, not evidence that the nondimensional parameter set represents a particular planet. Closure and interpretation limits The packaged model uses a naive relaxation closure: when heating adds layer mass, the corresponding active-layer momentum-exchange correction is omitted. It is a one-layer barotropic or 1.5-layer approximation; vertical shear, real radiative transfer, cloud feedback, and three-dimensional primitive-equation dynamics are outside it. This matters for scientific claims. The program's careful WASP-43b work found that a deformed single surface produces only a small geometry-induced latitudinal displacement under imposed symmetry breaking, with the converged sign differing from an early qualitative expectation. The actual planet's weak deformation makes the effect negligible, and richer models do not cleanly generate the observed -13.4^\circ latitude. The appropriate result is a bounded null, not a claim that shape explains the observation. Source trail Synthesized from , , , and the Phase-2/Phase-5 result summaries. See [[Verification ladder for BealeSurfaceSolver]] before reusing any reported number. Open questions Can the active-layer momentum source be added while retaining a clean energy and mass budget? Which semi-implicit or filtered wave step stabilizes extreme triaxial figures without reintroducing an arbitrary dissipation signal? Can the semi-Lagrangian core be promoted into the package with a verification suite that covers geometry, conservation, and forcing together? What is the minimal vertical model capable of addressing observations that the single surface provably cannot explain?

title: Geometry as forcing in planetary surface PDEs
deck: In Andrew's surface-PDE program, changing a world's figure changes the metric, differential operators, and normal-dependent forces, so geometry can alter dynamics even when the conventional forcing parameters are held fixed.
headings: Nulls and corrections are part of the thesis
text: In Andrew's surface-PDE program, changing a world's figure changes the metric, differential operators, and normal-dependent forces, so geometry can alter dynamics even when the conventional forcing parameters are held fixed. Up: [[BealeSurfaceSolver research (MOC)]] What “forcing” means here The phrase does not mean that curvature is always an extra body-force vector. It means that the geometry enters load-bearing parts of the PDE: \nabla_\Gamma\cdot v =\frac1{\sqrt g}\partial_i(\sqrt g,v^i), \qquad \Delta_\Gamma u =\frac1{\sqrt g}\partial_i(\sqrt g,g^{ij}\partial_j u), f_\Gamma=2\Omega\cdot n. Changing the surface changes \sqrt g , g^{ij} , and n . It therefore changes transport distances, modal spectra, wave propagation, Coriolis organization, and flux convergence before any radiative, stochastic, or mechanical forcing coefficient is changed. The strongest experiment holds everything else fixed and changes only the figure. A second control rescales the figures to equal area when total size could otherwise confound the comparison. The claim should then be stated as an operator or geometry effect, not as “shape alone creates weather” in every model. Positive examples in the repository Spectral fingerprints On the sphere, Laplace–Beltrami eigenvalues have rotational degeneracies. A triaxial figure breaks the symmetry and splits those multiplets. This is a particularly clean geometry signal because it can be checked against the known sphere ladder and does not depend on an arbitrary weather forcing. Energy-balance climate In the repository's Budyko–Sellers-style energy-balance model, (B I-D\Delta_\Gamma)T=Qas(x)-A, the oblate surface changes lateral heat transport through \Delta_\Gamma . An early comparison overstated the effect by also changing total area. After an equal-area correction, the recorded c/a=0.8 experiment still shows about a 29.9\% reduction in pole-to-equator temperature contrast and a poleward ice-line displacement in the tested parameter sets. The corrected result is stronger epistemically because it survived removal of a real confound. Hotspot and wave organization In forced shallow water, figure changes can move gyres, jets, or a hotspot while leaving the overall day-night amplitude nearly unchanged. This separates two questions: radiative and drag timescales largely set how much contrast survives, while geometry can influence where patterns sit. The observed effect depends on symmetry breaking, diagnostic choice, resolution, and model closure. Oblate brown dwarfs The flagship self-luminous experiment goes one step further. Its effective-potential gradient supplies both geometry and a gravity-darkened equilibrium target. A lever matrix separates the metric/normal effect from the thermal forcing effect. See [[One gradient two physics in oblate brown-dwarf weather]]. Nulls and corrections are part of the thesis Geometry is not automatically the dominant lever. The repository's converged single-surface WASP-43b investigation records a small displacement with a corrected sign and concludes that the planet's weak real deformation cannot explain the reported -13.4^\circ latitude. A richer model also fails to generate the observation without an external symmetry-breaking seed. The scientific statement is therefore bounded: geometry produces a measurable model effect in some regimes, but it does not explain that particular observation. Similarly, the brown-dwarf lever matrix reports that gravity-darkening forcing supplies most of the deterministic pole-equator contrast, while geometry mainly shifts a jet band. In that setting geometry is a modulator and coordinate structure, not the primary generator of thermal contrast. A disciplined experimental design A geometry-as-forcing claim is strongest when it includes: a sphere regression through the same general operator; an equal-area or otherwise physically matched figure sequence; a manufactured-solution convergence table on every geometry used; a forcing-only, geometry-only, both, and neither lever matrix where the model permits it; a diagnostic whose coordinate definition is consistent across figures; resolution and stencil-regime sensitivity; a statement of whether the result is a numerical mechanism, a physical forecast, or an observational inference. This turns “shape matters” from a slogan into a falsifiable program: it identifies the term through which shape enters, predicts which observable should move, and names the null experiment that would make the claim disappear. Source trail Synthesized from , , the Phase-1/2/3 result summaries, the equal-area EBM correction, the WASP-43b pipeline verdict, and the brown-dwarf capstones. Open questions Is there a dimensionless parameter that predicts when metric forcing competes with radiative, drag, or topographic forcing? Which observables are invariant enough across coordinate choices to compare strongly deformed figures fairly? Can shape-induced spectral splitting or achromatic phase signatures be isolated above realistic observational systematics? Where does geometry cease to be a perturbation and instead trigger a qualitative bifurcation in the dynamics?

title: Level-set geometry for surface conservation laws
deck: For a surface written as \phi=0 , its normal, chart area factor, conservative divergence, and Coriolis parameter can all be computed from the first derivative \nabla\phi .
headings: A graph chart from an implicit surface
The sphere is an algebraic regression test
A caveat about the level-set representation
text:
For a surface written as \phi=0 , its normal, chart area factor, conservative divergence, and Coriolis parameter can all be computed from the first derivative 
abla\phi . Up: [[BealeSurfaceSolver research (MOC)]] · Background: [[Beale cut-point method for surface PDEs]] A graph chart from an implicit surface Consider the chart in which the surface is locally z=z(x,y) . Differentiating \phi(x,y,z(x,y))=0 gives z_x=- rac{\phi_x}{\phi_z},\qquad z_y=- rac{\phi_y}{\phi_z}. The tangent basis is X_1=(1,0,z_x) and X_2=(0,1,z_y) . Its metric determinant is g=1+z_x^2+z_y^2. Substitution produces the useful identity \sqrt g = rac{\lVert
abla\phiVert}{|\phi_z|}. In the other two charts, the denominator is the component of 
abla\phi along the locally hidden coordinate. Thus the general expression is \sqrt g= rac{\lVert
abla\phiVert}{|\phi_
u|}. No Hessian of \phi is required. The admissibility condition |n_
u|\ge\eta implies \sqrt g\le1/\eta , so the same chart filter that avoids vertical graphs also bounds the area factor. Conservative surface divergence If a tangential vector field has contravariant chart components v^1,v^2 , then 
abla_\Gamma\cdot v = rac{1}{\sqrt g}\partial_i(\sqrt g\,v^i). The repository's preferred geometry-general route is therefore to multiply each flux component by \sqrt g , difference the weighted flux on the Cartesian chart, and divide by \sqrt g . For a conserved scalar q , \partial_t q + rac{1}{\sqrt g}\left[ \partial_1(\sqrt g F^1) +\partial_2(\sqrt g F^2) ight] =S. This is more than a convenient formula. It places the geometry inside the flux in the same way that a curvilinear-grid Jacobian enters a finite-volume conservation law. A spatially varying area factor can redirect or concentrate transport even when the forcing parameters are unchanged. An equivalent expanded expression is 
abla_\Gamma\cdot v =\partial_1v^1+\partial_2v^2 +(\partial_1\log\sqrt g)v^1 +(\partial_2\log\sqrt g)v^2. The last two terms are the connection contribution. In the research program they motivate the phrase [[Geometry as forcing in planetary surface PDEs]]: a changing metric alters a conservation law even without adding an external body force. Normal, tangent projection, and Coriolis The outward unit normal is n= rac{
abla\phi}{\lVert
abla\phiVert}. Any ambient vector a can be projected into the tangent plane by P_\Gamma a=a-(a\cdot n)n. Writing velocities as three-component Cartesian vectors and reprojecting them avoids carrying separate Christoffel-symbol formulas in each chart. For a rotating body with angular-velocity vector \Omega , the local Coriolis parameter is f_\Gamma(x)=2\Omega\cdot n(x). On a unit sphere rotating around the z axis, n=x and this reduces to 2\Omega z=2\Omega\sin\vartheta , the usual spherical expression. The sphere is an algebraic regression test For \phi=x^2+y^2+z^2-1, one has \lVert
abla\phiVert=2 and \phi_z=2z , so \sqrt g=1/|z| in the z chart. Then \partial_x\log\sqrt g= rac{x}{z^2},\qquad \partial_y\log\sqrt g= rac{y}{z^2}, which reproduces the sphere-specific geometric terms in Beale's shallow-water equations. This exact reduction is a strong design test: the general code path should recover the specialized sphere path up to discretization-level differences, not merely show qualitative similarity. A caveat about the level-set representation The zero set is unchanged if \phi is replaced by a nonzero scalar multiple or another function with the same zero set, while \lVert
abla\phiVert generally changes. Pure geometry must therefore depend on representation-invariant combinations such as the normalized normal and the ratio \lVert
abla\phiVert/|\phi_
u| . The oblate brown-dwarf program deliberately uses an effective-potential level set in a second, physical role: there \lVert
abla\phiVert is interpreted as effective gravity. That interpretation is justified only because \phi has physical normalization, not merely because it defines the correct surface. See [[One gradient two physics in oblate brown-dwarf weather]]. Source trail Synthesized from , , , and the mathematical layer of . Open questions Can a discrete geometric-conservation law be stated and proved for time-dependent level sets rebuilt from cut points? Which flux differencing choice best balances conservation, second-order accuracy, and robustness at chart seams? How should physical potentials be normalized so that \lVert
abla\phiVert has an unambiguous interpretation across models? Can the metric weights and tangent projections be combined into a structure-preserving discretization for fully nonlinear conservation laws?

title: Verification ladder for BealeSurfaceSolver
deck: BealeSurfaceSolver results are most credible when they climb from algebraic identities and exact benchmarks through convergence, conservation, ablations, independent reruns, and finally domain-specific interpretation.
headings: Failure evidence is part of verification
text: BealeSurfaceSolver results are most credible when they climb from algebraic identities and exact benchmarks through convergence, conservation, ablations, independent reruns, and finally domain-specific interpretation. Up: [[BealeSurfaceSolver research (MOC)]] Why a ladder is necessary A simulation that stays finite is not necessarily accurate, and an accurate PDE discretization does not automatically validate a scientific interpretation. The repository mixes package code, standalone research modules, result ledgers, manuscripts, and exploratory plans. Each layer answers a different question. A useful evidence ladder is: Code-path inspection — is the claimed equation actually implemented? Algebraic regression — does the general expression reduce to a known special case? Exact or manufactured solution — does the discrete error converge at the expected order? Conservation or budget closure — does the scheme respect the invariant or source balance relevant to the model? Nulls and ablations — does the signal vanish when its proposed mechanism is removed? Resolution and parameter robustness — does it persist beyond one grid and one tuning choice? Independent verification — can someone other than the result's producer recompute it from saved artifacts or a cold run? Scientific calibration — are units, physical parameters, observational degeneracies, and model limitations treated honestly? No later rung repairs a missing earlier one. A visually compelling flow field cannot substitute for a manufactured-solution test, and second-order convergence cannot establish that a one-layer atmosphere represents a real planet. Algebraic and benchmark anchors The geometry-general shallow-water path has a clean spherical limit. For the unit sphere, the normal, metric area factor, Coriolis parameter, and weighted-flux divergence reduce to Beale's sphere formulas. In recorded Williamson-2 runs, the generic path gives Resolution Generic L_2(\Phi) Beale table value N=80 1.115\times10^{-2} 1.13\times10^{-2} N=160 2.991\times10^{-3} 3.03\times10^{-3} The generic and specialized implementations differ at the scale expected from their finite-difference realizations, and the difference shrinks under refinement. This checks implementation consistency; it is not yet an off-sphere accuracy result. The diffusion and Laplace–Beltrami paths also reproduce sphere eigenvalues and published diffusion tables in the repository's verification routines. These are strong anchors because the exact structure is known before the experiment is run. Manufactured solutions off the sphere When no natural exact solution exists on an ellipsoid, the repository uses the method of manufactured solutions: choose a smooth field u^* , insert it into the continuous equation, and define the residual as a forcing so that u^* is exact by construction. Refining the cut-point grid then tests the operator independently of the scientific forcing. For geometry-general shallow water, the research records approximately 1.94 – 2.00 order in geopotential and momentum on sphere, oblate, and strongly triaxial test surfaces. Non-sphericity raises the error constant but does not erase the measured second-order trend in the tested range. The day-night equilibrium \max(0,n\cdot\hat s) is a deliberate counterexample to naive order claims: it has a kink at the terminator. The recorded order falls when that kink is unresolved and returns toward two when a grid-resolved smooth transition is used. The lesson is general: an operator's formal order cannot outrun the regularity of its data. Conservation and structure Different equations require different budgets: diffusion should dissipate an appropriate norm; unforced shallow water should control total layer mass and, depending on the formulation, energy or potential-vorticity quantities; forced-damped flow should close the balance between resolved tendency and explicit source or sink; reaction–diffusion should preserve physical bounds only if the numerical method actually has that property; moving-surface problems need a geometric-conservation accounting as well as a field equation. The repository uses an Appendix-B cut-point quadrature to approximate surface integrals. Some standalone research modules report machine-level mass fixes or machine-level energy and enstrophy drift in specially constructed structure-preserving schemes. Those statements belong to those modules and their tested configurations; they should not be silently transferred to the default MacCormack solver. Ablations that support causal interpretation The most informative experiments change one lever at a time. Examples recorded in the repository include: sphere versus non-spherical geometry at fixed forcing; one-gradient gravity-darkened forcing versus a flat-forcing control on the same oblate surface; \beta=0 in the brown-dwarf equilibrium target, which removes gravity-darkening contrast; equal-area versus unequal-area oblate climate comparisons, which exposed and corrected a size confound; cloud-off, still-atmosphere, and no-geometry controls in later brown-dwarf work; stable states versus diverged triaxial Jacobi states, where a NaN result is explicitly not interpreted as a physical absence of superrotation. These controls are more valuable than a larger catalog of unablated simulations because they discriminate mechanism from correlation. Failure evidence is part of verification Several negative results define the method's boundary: a coarse distorted ellipsoid can lack enough admissible cut-point neighbors; mixed-sign equilibration prevents a general M-matrix or positivity guarantee, and a reaction–diffusion path exhibited overshoot; the default hyperbolic core needs numerical stabilization; a viscosity-free centered wave step retains a checkerboard mode; exact Jacobi-figure weather experiments can diverge even when the equilibrium figure itself is computed accurately; the single-surface geometry mechanism does not explain WASP-43b's reported off-equatorial hotspot. Recording these failures prevents the success of one PDE family from being generalized to every surface, resolution, or physical regime. Provenance levels for Rome This import uses four practical labels when reading repository material: Package capability: exported under and covered by or a package verification path. Validated research implementation: a standalone driver with a stated analytic, manufactured, conservation, or ablation gate and saved evidence. Working result: recorded in a capstone, ledger, or manuscript but still inside an active working tree. Proposal or frontier: a question, planned mechanism, or extrapolation not yet established by a passing computation. The source documents often report a green test suite and independent verifier/blesser workflow. This Rome import inspected those records but did not rerun the large Julia research campaign. Their numerical values should therefore be described as repository-recorded results until independently reproduced from a frozen revision. Source trail Synthesized from , , , , the implementation-campaign summaries, the brown-dwarf claims workflow, and the program capstones. Open questions Which minimal cold-reproduction suite should freeze the strongest paper claims at a tagged commit? Can every paper figure be regenerated from a manifest that records code revision, parameters, seed, and data hash? Which conservation laws can be proved for the discrete operators rather than only measured numerically? How should the repository distinguish a failed physical hypothesis from a numerical method that failed before reaching the relevant regime?

title: What is String Theory
deck: One line: A framework proposing that nature's fundamental constituents aren't point particles but tiny vibrating one-dimensional strings , whose different vibration modes appear to us as the different particles.
text: What is String Theory One line: A framework proposing that nature's fundamental constituents aren't point particles but tiny vibrating one-dimensional strings , whose different vibration modes appear to us as the different particles. The core idea In the Standard Model, an electron or a quark is a mathematical point — zero size. String theory replaces each point with a string roughly the Planck length (~10⁻³⁵ m), far too small to see directly. Like a violin string, it can vibrate in different modes, and each mode looks like a different particle with a particular mass and charge. So one kind of object, vibrating differently, could in principle reproduce the whole particle zoo. Why physicists care A string's vibration spectrum automatically includes a massless spin-2 mode — and a massless spin-2 particle is exactly what a graviton (the quantum of gravity) must be. Gravity falls out of the theory rather than being bolted on, which is why string theory is the leading candidate for [[The graviton and quantum gravity|quantum gravity]] — uniting general relativity with quantum mechanics. It is highly constrained: mathematical consistency forces specific features (see below) rather than letting you tune anything. The strings attached (the hard parts) Extra dimensions. Consistency requires more than the 3+1 spacetime dimensions we observe — 26 for the early bosonic string, 10 for superstring theory. The extra ones are presumed curled up too small to notice → [[Why string theory needs extra dimensions]]. Five theories, then M-theory. There were five consistent superstring theories; in the 1990s they were shown to be limits of a single 11-dimensional framework, M-theory → [[M-theory and the five string theories]]. No experimental confirmation. The natural energy scale is the Planck scale, hopelessly beyond current colliders. As of now there is no direct experimental evidence, which is the central criticism of the program. The landscape. The extra dimensions can curl up in a staggering number of ways (~10⁵⁰⁰ estimates), each giving different physics — so the theory struggles to predict our universe uniquely → [[The landscape problem]]. Open questions (for me to chase) Why does consistency force exactly 10 dimensions? What breaks otherwise? What does "supersymmetry" add over the bosonic string, concretely? Is there any near-term experiment that could falsify it?

title: 2027 French presidential candidate field
deck: France's 2027 presidential field contains declared and party-selected contenders, but no one is yet a legally qualified candidate; every name must be read through dated evidence, coalition control, and the later 500-presentation process.
headings: The left: selection disputes before status inflation
Qualification is a later official event
text: France's 2027 presidential field contains declared and party-selected contenders, but no one is yet a legally qualified candidate; every name must be read through dated evidence, coalition control, and the later 500-presentation process. Up: [[2027 French presidential election]] · Related: [[2027 French presidential coalition map]] · [[The 500 presentations in French presidential elections]] · [[French presidential nomination mechanisms]] Status is evidence, not prominence French pre-campaign coverage often uses candidat loosely for anyone expected to run. This ledger uses narrower labels because they answer different questions. Discussed means that media, allies, or pollsters mention a person without a personal declaration. Exploring means that the person is taking identifiable organizational steps while withholding a declaration. Declared means that the person has personally and unambiguously said that they intend to contest the presidency. Party-selected means that a party or participating alliance has completed a procedure that gives the person its nomination. Qualified is reserved for the list later established by the Conseil constitutionnel after the presentation and eligibility process. These labels are cumulative only in a limited sense. A party-selected person has normally also declared, but selection does not create legal ballot access. A declared person can later withdraw. A court judgment, party vote, or coalition agreement can materially change a path without moving the person into the next legal category. No one should be described as an “official candidate” merely because a poll includes the name, a party leader endorses it, or a campaign says it has promises from 500 elected officials. Evidence ledger Person Current status Dated basis What the label does not establish Marine Le Pen Declared After the Paris Court of Appeal ruling on 7 July 2026, Le Pen said that she would run and continue her cassation appeal; Reuters reported that the unsuspended period of ineligibility imposed on appeal had already been served. Qualification, final disposition of litigation, or automatic RN control of every adjacent right-wing vote. Gabriel Attal Declared Attal held his first rally as a presidential candidate on 30 May 2026; Renaissance's own local federation records the campaign launch, while contemporaneous reporting identifies his candidacy explicitly. Selection by every party of the outgoing presidential coalition, acceptance of his proposed primary, or qualification. Édouard Philippe Declared Philippe publicly announced in September 2024 that he would be a candidate in the next presidential election; Horizons continues to organize an independent political offer around him. A joint center nomination, participation in a primary, or a settlement with Attal and other center-right figures. Bruno Retailleau Party-selected Retailleau declared on 12 February 2026. On 20 April, Les Républicains reported that 73.8% of participating members choosing among options favored designating the party president as its 2027 candidate. Legal qualification, the support of the entire conventional right, or withdrawal of neighboring center-right contenders. Jean-Luc Mélenchon Declared LFI proposed Mélenchon's candidacy for a 150,000-citizen investiture on 3 May 2026; in a 10 May interview he accepted the candidacy framing and said he considered himself capable, and his site describes the 7 June Saint-Denis meeting as the launch of LFI's 2027 campaign. Completion of LFI's proposed investiture, participation in a wider left primary, or qualification. Marine Tondelier Declared Les Écologistes selected Tondelier in December 2025 to represent the party in the left-and-ecologist primary; her official campaign site identifies her as a presidential candidate, and the party confirmed on 9 June 2026 that it would preserve her candidacy if the wider process failed. Victory in the proposed coalition primary, support from the whole left, or qualification. Raphaël Glucksmann Discussed His 2024 European result and Place publique leadership make him a recurring center-left possibility, but relevance and poll inclusion are not a personal declaration. Participation in or acceptance of a common-primary result, party selection, or qualification. François Ruffin Declared Ruffin announced on TF1 on 26 January 2026 that he was a candidate for the presidency and published the declaration on his official site the next day. Party or coalition selection, a binding common-left mechanism, or qualification. Fabien Roussel Discussed As PCF national secretary and its 2022 presidential candidate, Roussel is relevant to whether the communists run independently or join a selection process. A 2027 declaration or PCF nomination. Jordan Bardella Discussed Bardella is RN president and the party's obvious contingency if Le Pen cannot or does not run. Le Pen's July statement instead presented him as her intended prime minister. A presidential declaration, automatic substitution, legal qualification, or a binding promise of appointment to Matignon. The table is deliberately asymmetric. It records stronger labels only when the underlying act is direct and dated. It does not attempt to reward prominence with a higher status. It also does not treat every name tested by an institute as a candidate. Pollsters construct hypothetical slates to answer survey questions; they do not register candidacies. The nationalist-right branch Marine Le Pen is the declared RN path as of the research cutoff. Her status requires two qualifications. First, her declaration followed an appellate ruling whose legal consequences must be described precisely. Reuters reported that the Paris Court of Appeal upheld the conviction in the European Parliament assistants case, reduced the unsuspended ineligibility period to time already served, and left further cassation proceedings. The correct inference is that the appellate disposition presently leaves an electoral path. It is not that the conviction vanished or that later legal process is irrelevant. Second, Le Pen's declaration does not make Jordan Bardella a co-candidate or successor candidate. Her stated plan assigns Bardella a possible governing role. Under the Fifth Republic, however, a president appoints the prime minister in a parliamentary environment shaped by the National Assembly; a campaign announcement cannot guarantee a durable majority or appointment under every post-election configuration. [[From the Élysée to a National Assembly majority]] explains that separate test. Bardella remains important because party leadership, public profile, and previous polling make him the most obvious RN contingency. That is exactly why the label discussed matters: it can capture genuine strategic relevance without inventing a declaration. Poll scenarios substituting Bardella for Le Pen test a counterfactual field. They should not be averaged with Le Pen scenarios or reported as evidence that the substitution has occurred. The rest of the nationalist and sovereignist right cannot be compressed into the RN line. Éric Zemmour, Marion Maréchal, Nicolas Dupont-Aignan, and other figures or parties may be discussed, organize, endorse, or contest independently. Each needs its own direct evidence before entering this canonical ledger at exploring or declared status. Ideological adjacency does not create shared nomination authority, and an eventual endorsement would not guarantee complete voter transfer. The post-Macron succession branch Emmanuel Macron cannot serve a third consecutive term under Article 6 of the Constitution, so the outgoing governing space has no incumbent nomination to inherit. Gabriel Attal and Édouard Philippe are declared contenders with different organizational bases and different theories of legitimacy. Attal leads Renaissance and has advocated a selection process capable of consolidating the center. Philippe leads Horizons and has resisted making his candidacy dependent on such a primary. That disagreement is substantive. A primary could create a shared result only for organizations and candidates that agree on its electorate, eligibility rules, timetable, and binding force. If Philippe does not participate, an Attal victory would not automatically demote Philippe from declared status. Conversely, Philippe's earlier declaration does not give Horizons authority over Renaissance, MoDem, or the wider center-right. The field can therefore contain more than one declared successor even when commentators speak of a single bloc central . Other figures associated with the outgoing majority or center-right should be handled cautiously. Holding a senior office, creating a political association, publishing a program, or appearing in a poll may support exploring if it is tied to identifiable presidential organization. Otherwise the person remains discussed . The threshold prevents a succession story from becoming a list of every prominent minister. The institutional resource behind this branch is broader than its polling percentage. Renaissance, Horizons, MoDem, and allied networks contain parliamentarians, local officeholders, donors, and campaign professionals. Those assets can assist with presentations and national organization. They do not settle which declared person receives them, and they cannot turn a coalition label into a legal nomination. Les Républicains: declaration plus selection Bruno Retailleau currently has the strongest party-procedural label in the field. His 12 February statement plainly meets the declaration test. Les Républicains then asked members about the method of choosing the party's candidate. The party's 20 April report says turnout was 60.01% and, among members choosing between the proposed methods, 73.8% favored designating the party president; smaller shares preferred closed or sympathizer-open primaries. LR described the result as designating Retailleau as the movement's candidate. That is sufficient for party-selected in this ledger, even though the consultation asked members to choose a procedure rather than staging a conventional multicandidate primary. The label records the party's own completed act and stated effect. It does not settle whether other right-wing organizations accept the result or whether a later bargain alters the field. Retailleau's selection also demonstrates why the ledger separates organization from public support. A party can confer a real nomination while its candidate remains weaker in hypothetical national surveys. Conversely, a highly placed person can poll strongly without controlling a party procedure. Both facts matter, but they answer different questions. The left: selection disputes before status inflation The left's central uncertainty is not just which personality is most popular. It is whether any process can bind organizations with different programs and strategic goals. LFI can argue that Mélenchon's three prior candidacies, activist infrastructure, and 2022 vote establish a focal point. Ecologists and other participants can argue for an open or common selection. Social democrats can reject both an LFI-led convergence and a procedure whose boundaries they do not control. Jean-Luc Mélenchon now meets the declared threshold. LFI's 3 May proposal of his candidacy to a 150,000-citizen investiture, his own 10 May acceptance of the candidacy framing, and the movement's June campaign launch are stronger than observer expectation. The investiture's completion remains a separate party-procedural event; declaration does not permit the ledger to assume it. Marine Tondelier is declared and is the Ecologists' selected representative in the proposed wider primary. This ledger reserves party-selected for the person chosen as a party's or alliance's presidential nominee, rather than a party representative entering a still-unfinished coalition selection. If she wins that binding wider vote—or if the Ecologists formally convert their representative designation into an autonomous presidential nomination—the stronger label becomes appropriate. François Ruffin likewise meets the declared threshold through his January announcement. Raphaël Glucksmann, Fabien Roussel, and other relevant left figures should be treated in the same disciplined way. European-election performance, an association, speaking tours, programmatic positioning, or allies urging a run can establish political relevance. Only direct acts establish the stronger categories. A common primary, if held, would select a candidate only within the scope of participating organizations; it could not erase a nonparticipant's declaration. Qualification is a later official event No person in this ledger is qualified . Under the legal framework explained in [[The 500 presentations in French presidential elections]], a prospective candidate needs at least 500 valid presentations from eligible officeholders, distributed across at least 30 departments or overseas units and respecting the concentration rule. Forms must be received and validated through the election-specific process. The Conseil constitutionnel then establishes the candidate list. Before that window, campaigns may announce pledges or claim that they have enough parrainages . Such claims can be useful evidence of organization, but they are not certified totals. Even a party-selected contender with a dense local network must complete the legal process. Conversely, a smaller party can qualify through disciplined territorial work despite modest polling. The same caution applies to eligibility litigation. A court ruling may remove or restore a plausible route, but the canonical status should describe what the ruling actually does, any suspensive appeal, and the remaining official steps. Legal possibility is not qualification; unresolved risk is not automatic disqualification. How this ledger should change Update a row only for a traceable status event: a personal declaration, an explicit withdrawal, a completed party or alliance procedure, a consequential final or operative court ruling, or the Conseil constitutionnel's official list. Preserve the old status and transition date in prose rather than silently rewriting history. Add a new person when direct evidence establishes at least exploring status or when the person is essential to understanding a live succession or selection contingency. Do not update for an anonymous report alone, a poll's tested slate, a television host's prediction, an ally's wish, or a campaign appearance that never states presidential intent. Multiple articles repeating the same anonymous briefing remain one unconfirmed claim. When French wording is ambiguous— candidat naturel , prêt , disponible , or vocation à —quote or translate narrowly and wait for an unmistakable act. The ledger also should not become a forecast table. Status describes verified procedural position. Viability requires separate analysis of first-round support, ballot access, coalition breadth, runoff expansion, finance, and capacity to govern. [[2027 French presidential coalition map]] owns that larger structure, while [[How to read French presidential polls]] explains why tested scenarios cannot be collapsed into a ranking of actual candidates. Why it matters Candidate-status discipline prevents three recurrent errors. It stops hypothetical polling from manufacturing candidacies. It stops party declarations from being mistaken for official ballot access. And it stops political relevance from being translated into a false claim that a person has personally chosen to run. The result is not merely semantic caution. Different statuses imply different failure modes. A discussed figure may never enter. An exploring figure may lose or abandon a selection process. A declared contender may fail to consolidate a party or collect valid presentations. A party-selected contender may still confront litigation, finance, or qualification barriers. A qualified candidate may still lack a plausible runoff or governing coalition. Keeping the categories separate makes later changes legible instead of forcing every development into “in” or “out.” Sources Les Républicains, “Je suis candidat à l’élection présidentielle” — Retailleau's direct declaration, February 12, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Les Républicains, member consultation result — turnout, option shares, and party description of Retailleau's designation, April 20, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Renaissance Seine-et-Marne federation — records the May 30, 2026 launch of Gabriel Attal's campaign; accessed July 10, 2026. Le Monde, “Gabriel Attal declares his candidacy” — contemporaneous secondary confirmation of Attal's declaration; accessed July 10, 2026. Reuters, reporting on Édouard Philippe's declaration — September 3, 2024; accessed July 10, 2026. Reuters report syndicated by Investing.com, “French court opens door to possible Le Pen presidential run” — appellate ruling, July 7, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Reuters report syndicated by MarketScreener, “Marine Le Pen says she will run for president in 2027” — declaration and cassation appeal, July 7, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Les Écologistes, Tondelier internal designation — party representative for the proposed primary; accessed July 10, 2026. Les Écologistes, political-bureau communiqué — June 9, 2026 primary position and fallback candidacy; accessed July 10, 2026. Marine Tondelier official campaign site — candidate identification and campaign material; accessed July 10, 2026. La France insoumise, intergroup declaration — proposal of Mélenchon's candidacy to a 150,000-citizen investiture, May 3, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, candidacy interview — direct acceptance of the candidacy framing, May 10, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, Saint-Denis campaign launch — LFI 2027 presidential-campaign launch, June 7, 2026; accessed July 10, 2026. Open questions What event will complete or supersede LFI's proposed citizen-investiture process for Mélenchon? Which organizations will participate in, and promise to respect, the proposed left-and-ecologist selection? Will the post-Macron center agree on any binding selection mechanism before strategic voting begins to consolidate the field informally? When will the Conseil constitutionnel publish the election-specific presentation calendar and live validation interface for 2027?

title: 2027 French presidential coalition map
deck: France's 2027 presidential field is organized by competing coalition projects, but a presidential coalition is a sequence of coordination problems—not a fixed transfer of party votes to one candidate.
headings: Rassemblement National and the nationalist right
Les Républicains and the conventional right
The fragmented left and rival routes to unity
Ecologists, social democrats, and the center-left hinge
Smaller candidacies are part of the mechanism
text: France's 2027 presidential field is organized by competing coalition projects, but a presidential coalition is a sequence of coordination problems—not a fixed transfer of party votes to one candidate. Up: [[2027 French presidential election]] · Related: [[How the French presidential election works]] · [[From the Élysée to a National Assembly majority]] · [[2027 French presidential candidate field]] How to read this map The useful unit in a French presidential pre-campaign is neither the individual name alone nor a permanent party “bloc.” It is a coalition project : an attempt to combine a candidate, participating organizations, elected officials, activists, money, access to the 500 presentations, and voters who may behave differently in the two rounds. The projects below describe the field as of 9 July 2026. They are analytical families, not a prediction that each will produce exactly one ballot line. Three distinctions prevent false certainty. First, a party alliance in the [[National Assembly of France|National Assembly]] is not automatically a presidential alliance. Legislative coalitions divide 577 constituency nominations and can tolerate several national personalities. A presidential election selects one person on one national ballot. The choice of candidate therefore concentrates disputes about leadership, program, and strategy that a parliamentary arrangement can postpone. Second, a declared candidacy is not a qualified candidacy. Marine Le Pen, Gabriel Attal, Édouard Philippe, Bruno Retailleau, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, and other figures may announce that they intend to run, but only the Conseil constitutionnel's later list establishes who has satisfied the legal gateway described in [[The 500 presentations in French presidential elections]]. This note maps political coordination; it does not confer official status. Third, first-round coordination and second-round transfer are different mechanisms. A party can withdraw its own contender and still fail to deliver all of its electorate to the endorsed person. Conversely, voters can converge on a candidate through a vote utile —a strategic “useful vote”—without a formal party agreement. The runoff then creates a new binary choice in which abstention, blank voting, and rejection of the opposing finalist matter alongside endorsement. Rassemblement National and the nationalist right The Rassemblement National (RN) begins with the most centralized large coalition project. Its core combines the party organization, a disciplined national brand, a substantial parliamentary presence, Marine Le Pen's long presidential record, and Jordan Bardella's leadership profile. The central coordination problem is consequently less about holding an open primary than about the allocation of roles at the top. That allocation changed materially on 7 July 2026. The Paris Court of Appeal upheld Le Pen's conviction in the European Parliament assistants case but reduced the unsuspended portion of the ineligibility sentence to a period Reuters reported had already been served; her further appeal suspends the appellate ruling while cassation is pending. Le Pen then said she would run, pursue that appeal, and campaign with Bardella as her intended prime minister. The legally careful description is therefore: Le Pen is declared , the appellate sentence presently leaves a path to the election, and further litigation creates residual uncertainty. It would be inaccurate either to describe her as already qualified or to write that all legal uncertainty has disappeared. This proposed Le Pen–Bardella division also reveals why a presidential coalition cannot be evaluated only through first-round polls. A national candidate needs an account of governing personnel and a path through the Assembly. Naming Bardella for Matignon can signal continuity and mobilize his supporters, but the president cannot award a durable legislative majority by announcement. [[From the Élysée to a National Assembly majority]] explains the separate parliamentary test. The RN's outer boundary remains a political question. Allies to its right or drawn from the traditional right may support the same presidential contender, compete independently, or bargain over later legislative nominations. Éric Zemmour's Reconquête and smaller sovereignist candidacies can appeal to partially overlapping voters without belonging to the RN organization. A poll that places them on separate first-round lines does not measure the share of a single transferable nationalist bloc; a poll that omits them tests a different choice architecture. The post-Macron center and center-right The space built around Emmanuel Macron faces a succession problem because Article 6 of the Constitution bars a third consecutive presidential term. The organizations associated with the outgoing majority—notably Renaissance, Horizons, MoDem, and smaller allied formations—retain elected officials and governing experience, but they do not inherit a constitutionally designated nominee. Gabriel Attal and Édouard Philippe illustrate two rival methods of consolidation. Attal, the Renaissance leader and former prime minister, declared his candidacy in May 2026. Philippe, former prime minister and leader of Horizons, had declared earlier. Public Sénat reported in June that a liaison committee acknowledged disagreement between them over a possible primary: Attal defended a selection mechanism while Philippe rejected that route. That is not a minor procedural quarrel. A primary can create a visible winner and common campaign, but it also defines who may vote, which parties accept the result, and whether candidates from the traditional right participate. Refusing it preserves a candidate's independent mandate while risking several adjacent first-round lines. The phrase “central bloc” can also conceal a programmatic tension. Some potential partners define the project as continuity with the reformist, pro-European Macron coalition. Others want a broader right-and-center agreement that places immigration, security, public spending, or institutional authority nearer the center of gravity. Still others fear that a pre-election bargain with Les Républicains would erase the identity that separated Macronism from the traditional right. Coalition breadth can therefore reduce fragmentation while increasing internal vetoes. There is no reliable arithmetic in which the prior votes of Renaissance, Horizons, MoDem, or a center-right candidate simply add together. Their electorates overlap but are not identical. Candidate image, incumbent-government responsibility, and the tested field affect whether voters remain, defect right, move toward a social-democratic option, or abstain. The live question is whether this family can create a focal candidacy before strategic voting creates one from below. Les Républicains and the conventional right Les Républicains (LR) occupies a difficult position between organizational autonomy and electoral overlap with both the post-Macron center and the RN. Bruno Retailleau declared his candidacy in February 2026. Other figures on the conventional right have also been discussed or have developed their own political vehicles. The durable coalition question is whether LR seeks its own presidential line, participates in a wider right-and-center selection, or fragments across candidates who offer different relationships to Macronism and the RN. The party has resources that raw national polling can understate: local elected officials, territorial organization, parliamentary experience, and potential presentation networks. But those assets do not themselves solve the first-round coordination problem. A candidate may possess credible ballot access yet struggle to become the strategic choice of right-leaning voters. Conversely, a centrist contender might attract some LR voters without securing party leaders, activists, or legislative cooperation. Calling the entire space “the right” therefore collapses three choices. There is a choice of candidate; a choice about whether the governing break is primarily with Macronism or with the RN; and a choice about post-presidential legislative cooperation. These choices can point in different directions. A presidential endorsement may be easier than a common program, while an agreement over program may still founder on leadership. The fragmented left and rival routes to unity The left contains the clearest example of a legislative coalition failing to settle presidential leadership. The Nouveau Front populaire created rapid constituency coordination for the 2024 legislative election among La France insoumise (LFI), the Parti socialiste (PS), Les Écologistes, and the Parti communiste français (PCF). That agreement demonstrated the ability to avoid some first-round legislative competition. It did not create a permanent organization or an uncontested method for choosing one presidential candidate. At least three presidential strategies now overlap. One is the LFI route , centered on Jean-Luc Mélenchon and the movement's own program, activist structure, and electoral base. LFI has resisted a selection process in which other organizations could determine its nominee or dilute its program. Its leverage rests partly on Mélenchon's prior first-round strength and the argument that convergence should occur behind the best-established left candidacy. Its constraint is that voters and organizations elsewhere on the left may reject both the candidate and the terms of that convergence. A second is the unitary-primary route associated with Les Écologistes and other participating organizations. An official Ecologists statement on 9 June 2026 reaffirmed support for a primary of the left and ecologists and put the proposal to members, while preserving Marine Tondelier's candidacy if the process failed. Earlier Front Populaire 2027 material described a planned 11 October 2026 vote. The key analytical questions are participation, eligibility, voter registration, programmatic commitments, and whether absent organizations promise to respect the result. A primary can validly select a candidate among its participants without becoming a primary of the entire left. A third is an independent social-democratic or party route , potentially including figures associated with the PS or Place publique and others who may see a larger electorate between LFI and the center. Its argument is that left unity under an unacceptable platform can repel more voters than it combines. Its risk is duplication: several candidates can appeal to similar voters and each fall below a runoff threshold that a single candidacy might reach. The PCF and smaller far-left formations add further choices. Some value an autonomous first-round expression of program and organization; others may bargain for unity. The left's coalition map is thus not a clean binary between “unity” and “division.” It is a dispute over which voters define the coalition, which program binds it, how the candidate is selected, and whether legislative reciprocity follows. Ecologists, social democrats, and the center-left hinge Ecologists and social democrats deserve separate attention even when they participate in broader left processes because they can function as a hinge. Their voters may prioritize defeating the RN, maintaining a distinct ecological or pro-European program, avoiding LFI, or preventing capture by the outgoing center. Those motivations do not always nominate the same person. For Les Écologistes, the primary proposal creates an explicit contingency: attempt common selection, while retaining an autonomous candidate if agreement fails. That makes the participation rules and deadlines politically consequential, not administrative detail. For the PS, internal disagreements over government censure, relations with LFI, and the presidential route can affect both whether the party joins a primary and whether all of its currents accept the outcome. Place publique's relationship to a unitary process similarly matters because a candidate with a pro-European center-left profile may draw support from voters who would not back an LFI-led offer. This hinge also affects the post-Macron center. A center-left contender can draw disaffected governing-coalition voters without joining the outgoing majority. A centrist contender can seek social-democratic voters through a republican-front appeal against the RN or LFI. Such appeals are conditional and candidate-specific; they are not proof that a permanent “anti-extremist bloc” exists. Smaller candidacies are part of the mechanism Communist, far-left, sovereignist, regionalist, rural-interest, and single-issue candidacies should not be treated only as noise around four large families. A candidacy can influence the agenda, reveal a durable constituency, qualify for the higher campaign-reimbursement ceiling by crossing the statutory vote threshold, or alter which large candidate appears viable. Reimbursement remains conditional on compliant accounts; it is not an automatic grant for appearing on the ballot. Yet discussion is not ballot access. Smaller organizations face the same presentation, finance, and account requirements as larger ones, often with less margin for invalid forms or fundraising problems. The presence of a smaller candidate also changes poll interpretation. When an institute removes a name, supplies a different center candidate, or tests Le Pen rather than Bardella, it reallocates attention and choice rather than observing the same electorate under identical conditions. [[How to read French presidential polls]] should therefore be used before converting hypothetical slates into a coalition ranking. Five tests for coalition strength The apparent size of a coalition should be checked against five distinct capacities. Selection: Is there an accepted procedure or only competing declarations? A primary, congress, party endorsement, negotiated withdrawal, and strategic-voter convergence are different mechanisms. Qualification: Does the prospective candidate have a credible path to 500 valid, geographically distributed presentations and the required declarations? Party popularity is not enough. First-round mobilization: Can the coalition turn sympathy into valid votes under the tested slate, including turnout and competition from adjacent candidates? Runoff expansion: Can the finalist attract voters who did not support the coalition in round one without demobilizing the core? Endorsements are evidence of elite choice, not guaranteed transfer rates. Governing extension: Can the presidential project support a government in the Assembly? A broad negative coalition against an opponent may win the Élysée while remaining too thin for 289 deputies. These capacities can move independently. A candidate can poll well but struggle with elected-official presentations. A disciplined party can qualify easily but fail to expand in the runoff. A broad second-round winner can enter office without a parliamentary majority. “Coalition strength” is therefore a vector, not one percentage. What would change the map The map should be revised after a binding selection result, verified withdrawal, party endorsement with clear scope, consequential court decision, new parliamentary alliance, or official qualification evidence. It should not be rewritten for every anonymous report of negotiations. Near-term resolution points include the rules and participation of the proposed left primary; the center and center-right decision over a common selection method; any formal LR nomination procedure; the legal timetable of Le Pen's further appeal; and evidence that presidential coordination includes—or explicitly excludes—legislative reciprocity. Each event can narrow the field without guaranteeing that voters transfer as party leaders intend. Why it matters France's two-round presidency rewards coordination but does not make coalitions mechanical. Mapping only candidates turns institutions into personality drama. Mapping only parties ignores leadership and strategic voting. Mapping only polls treats hypothetical menus as durable blocs. A coalition map instead asks who can select, qualify, mobilize, expand, and govern. Those five tests explain why a crowded field can consolidate suddenly—and why apparent unity can fracture between the presidential first round, runoff, and Assembly. Sources Conseil constitutionnel, Constitution of 4 October 1958, Articles 6–8 and 20–21 , current text, accessed 2026-07-09. Legifrance, Law no. 62-1292 of 6 November 1962, consolidated text , presidential qualification and election framework, accessed 2026-07-09. Les Écologistes, Communiqué de presse du Bureau politique des Écologistes , 9 June 2026, accessed 2026-07-09. Front Populaire 2027 / Les Écologistes, Primary announcement and planned 11 October 2026 vote , accessed 2026-07-09. Reuters, French court opens door to possible Le Pen presidential run, with ankle tag , 7 July 2026, accessed 2026-07-09. Reuters, Political survivor Le Pen makes her boldest gamble yet for France's presidency , 8 July 2026, accessed 2026-07-09. Public Sénat, Le comité de liaison acte un désaccord Attal–Philippe sur une primaire , 10 June 2026, accessed 2026-07-09. LCP–Assemblée nationale, Présidentielle 2027: la liste des candidats déjà en lice et des prétendants , updated 7 July 2026, accessed 2026-07-09. Le Monde, 2027 French presidential election: declared and potential candidates , updated 7 July 2026, accessed 2026-07-09. Open questions Which organizations will formally participate in the proposed 11 October left primary, and what electorate and result-binding rules will apply? Will the post-Macron center adopt a binding selection method or allow strategic voting to choose among several declared candidates? How will the Cour de cassation timetable and any resulting judgment affect the precise legal description of Marine Le Pen's eligibility? Which presidential agreements will include reciprocal legislative nominations or an explicit governing coalition? Which original polling series can test coalition breadth while holding the candidate slate and turnout assumptions sufficiently stable?

title: 2027 French presidential election calendar
deck: France's Interior Ministry publishes 18 April and 2 May 2027 for the presidential ballots, but many other dates are only statutory calculations from that first-round date, while the convocation decree and election-specific decisions that will operationally settle the calendar have not yet been issued.
headings: From the ballot date to candidate qualification
Campaign finance is a different calendar
text: France's Interior Ministry publishes 18 April and 2 May 2027 for the presidential ballots, but many other dates are only statutory calculations from that first-round date, while the convocation decree and election-specific decisions that will operationally settle the calendar have not yet been issued. Up: [[2027 French presidential election]] The calendar at a glance The safest way to read the 2027 timetable is to separate five kinds of date that are often blurred together.
